sprint_name: Sprint 1 - Stop fee-dodging after acceptance (P0)
title: Stop fee-dodging after acceptance and give stalled projects a way out
headline: Stop winning firms dodging fees and unstick stalled projects
goal: Stop the winning firm from withdrawing and getting its credits back after the client accepts, and give clients, firms and admins a clear way to close a project that stalls or is never decided.
value: Winning firms pay their credits, and every stalled or undecided cerere ends with credits settled once.
do_first: Block claim withdrawals once the cerere is ACCEPTED or the slot's offer is accepted, with a test.
steps: Return CLAIM_NOT_WITHDRAWABLE from withdrawals after acceptance, and hide the withdraw button in the UI.
Build one settlement function that closes a project and refunds or consumes credits exactly once, per PO rules.
Add client 'Firma nu mai răspunde' report, firm mutual-cancel confirm, and an audited admin close on /admin/requests/[id].
Add a worker settling slots N days after offers expire, reminding the client beforehand; allow extension requests on expired offers.
Add an 'Acordul vostru' card, hide 'Ofertă expirată' on accepted offers, remind firm 3 days before delivery, flag overdue.
done_when: A winning firm can no longer withdraw its claim after the client accepts.
Admin can close a stalled project and see credits settled once in its timeline.
An undecided cerere with expired offers is settled automatically; both sides get notified.
decision_needed: When a project is cancelled after acceptance or the client never decides, after how many days, and are the firm's reserved credits refunded or consumed?
risks: The immediate withdrawal block is safe, but cancellation after acceptance, the client-decision timeout and the credit refund/consume rules are DECIZIE NECESARA for the PO. Settlement must go through one function so credits are never settled twice.
acceptance: WithdrawalsService.request returns CLAIM_NOT_WITHDRAWABLE once the request is ACCEPTED or later, or the slot's quote is ACCEPTED; a spec covers withdraw-after-accept and the UI hides the withdraw block
A client can report that a project has fallen through, which opens an admin case, and an admin can close the project through an audited action that settles credits once
Requests whose offers all expired without a decision close automatically after the PO-approved timeout and both sides are notified
The accepted offer card no longer shows 'Ofertă expirată', and the firm gets a reminder 3 days before the delivery date

findings.title: No way out of ACCEPTED when a project falls through: client cannot cancel or report, firms cannot mutually cancel, admin has no project controls
findings.description: After acceptance the winner's slot stays OFFER_SENT, and withdrawals are gated only on slot status. The winning firm can therefore auto-withdraw with CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, get its reserved claim credits refunded, then still markDelivered, and the project completes with zero credits consumed, which bypasses pay-to-play and strands the request in ACCEPTED. Beyond that exploit, no exit from ACCEPTED exists other than the winner marking delivery: the client cannot cancel or report, admin has no request/claim controls despite rule 4.19, and reconciliation ignores stale ACCEPTED requests. Fix now: block withdrawals once the request is ACCEPTED or later (S); then DECIZIE NECESARA from the PO on a 'cancelled after acceptance' outcome with credit settlement, plus client report and admin close actions.
findings.proposed_fix: DECIZIE NECESARA (PO): define a terminal 'project cancelled after acceptance' outcome and what happens to the winner's reserved credits (refund vs consume) in each case: mutual, firm fault, client fault. Then implement: a client action 'Firma nu mai raspunde / anuleaza proiectul', which opens an admin case and notifies the firm; firm confirmation for a mutual cancel; and /admin/requests/[id] with status, timeline, slots and credit movements, plus an audited 'close project' action that goes through a single settlement function like completeDelivered.

findings.title: No terminal state when the client never decides: offers expire, the request stays OFFERS_RECEIVED forever and firm credits stay reserved
findings.description: When the client never accepts, all quotes eventually go SENT->EXPIRED and nothing else changes: the request stays OFFERS_RECEIVED (shown under the client's "Active" tab) and each slot stays OFFER_SENT with its claim credits reserved. The status recompute counts EXPIRED quotes as still open, request-expiration only handles IN_MARKETPLACE, and the reconciliation sweep has no branch for these requests. The only exits are manual (a firm withdraws with CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H for a refund, extends or re-offers, or the client deletes the request), so the PO needs to decide on a client-decision timeout and whether slots are refunded or consumed, which the 2026-08-19 audit already flagged as DECIZIE NECESARA.
findings.proposed_fix: PO decision: e.g. N days after the last quote expires with no extension or new version, close the request (new status or EXPIRED), refund or consume the OFFER_SENT slots per the pay-to-play policy, and notify both sides. Remind the client to decide before the offers expire.

findings.title: Nothing surfaces the agreed terms or progress after acceptance: no price or delivery-date summary, no milestones, no due-date reminders
findings.description: After acceptance nothing tracks progress. No reminder fires as the offer's deliveryDate approaches or passes, IN_EXECUTION is never set, and a request whose firm never marks delivery stays ACCEPTED forever with no nudge, while the winner's credits stay RESERVED. The agreed terms are visible (the accepted OfferCard stays on both sides), but that card still shows 'Ofertă expirată' once the offer's validUntil passes, which mislabels the deal both sides agreed to. Proposed fix: hide the validity line on ACCEPTED quotes; add a delayed job and reconciliation sweep that reminds the firm at deliveryDate minus 3 days and flags the request as overdue to both sides after deliveryDate while it is not DELIVERED; and get a PO decision on whether a firm 'Am inceput executia' action (sets IN_EXECUTION) is wanted or the value is marked reserved.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an 'Acordul vostru' card on both sides (price and currency, delivery date or term, warranty, acceptedAt) built from the accepted version. Add an optional firm action 'Am inceput executia', which sets IN_EXECUTION with an ETA and notifies the client. Add a BullMQ reminder to the firm at deliveryDate minus 3 days and an 'intarziat' flag to both sides after deliveryDate while not DELIVERED, with the reconciliation sweep covering the reminder.

findings.title: Expired offers leave the cerere and the claim slot in limbo with no timeout or automatic exit
findings.description: When validity runs out, the only change is the quote going to EXPIRED. The slot stays OFFER_SENT, it keeps occupying one of the max slots, and its credits stay RESERVED. recomputeRequestStatusAfterClaimChange counts EXPIRED as an open offer, so the cerere stays OFFERS_RECEIVED/NEGOTIATION, and neither the request-expiry worker nor the reconciliation sweep touches that state. The client cannot accept, reject or ask for changes on an EXPIRED quote, so every exit is manual: the firm extends or re-offers, the firm withdraws the claim (refunded under CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, otherwise a voluntary withdrawal with penalty), or the client deletes the cerere. With nobody acting, the cerere never returns to the market, and the 'Ofertă expirată' penalty (3 points) in business rules 4.12 is never applied.
findings.proposed_fix: PO decision needed on the grace period, for example N days after the last quote expires with no extension or re-offer. When it passes, a worker closes the slot (for example CANCELLED_OFFER_EXPIRED with a refund or consume per pay-to-play) and calls recomputeRequestStatusAfterClaimChange so the cerere returns to IN_MARKETPLACE with a new expiry clock. Also let the client ask for an extension on an EXPIRED quote, and add this sweep to the reconciliation worker.

sprint_name: Sprint 1 - Stop fee-dodging after acceptance (P0)
title: Stop winning firms from withdrawing after the client accepts
headline: Stop firms from quitting after the client says yes
goal: Once a client accepts a firm's offer, that firm can no longer withdraw to get its credits back, and only the owner, a manager or the assigned person can withdraw a claim or mark a job delivered.
value: Clients keep their winning firma, and only owners or managers can withdraw claims or mark delivery.
do_first: Write a failing test where the winning firma withdraws with CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H after acceptance.
steps: Refuse claim withdrawal with 409 when the oferta or cerere is accepted or delivered, including admin paths.
Refuse mark-delivered unless the winning slot is still in offer-sent state.
Limit withdraw and mark-delivered to owner or manager; claimer or assignee may withdraw only within the 30-minute grace.
Hide the withdraw and deliver buttons for accepted oferte and for staff without permission.
Add test cases for each withdrawal reason by a winner and for managed employees.
done_when: Winning firma sees no 'Retrage preluarea' button after the client accepts.
Employee account sees no 'Marchează ca livrată' button.
Test report shows the new winner-withdrawal and employee cases passing.
risks: Firms that genuinely need to leave an accepted job will have no exit until a dedicated post-acceptance cancellation flow exists, so admins must handle those cases by hand for now.
acceptance: Withdrawing a claim whose quote is ACCEPTED, or whose request is ACCEPTED/DELIVERED, returns 409 for every reason (including CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H and admin approval), and no credits are refunded
markDelivered is refused when the winning slot is no longer OFFER_SENT
An EMPLOYEE_MANAGED member who is not the assignee gets FORBIDDEN on withdraw and deliver, and the buttons are hidden for them
Spec cases cover a winner withdrawing with each reason and a managed employee trying both actions

findings.title: The winning firm can still withdraw its claim after the client accepts, and even after delivery (it can refund its own credits and strands the client)
findings.description: After acceptance, and even after it marks the job delivered, the winning firm's slot stays OFFER_SENT, and withdrawals are gated only on the slot status. The winner can therefore withdraw with CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, which is auto-approved: the timer falls back to slot.createdAt when the client never used chat, and the withdrawal refunds all of its reserved credits. The ACCEPTED quote and request stay unchanged, the chat goes read-only, and the firm can still markDelivered, while completeDelivered skips the credit consumption because the slot is WITHDRAWN. The firm gets the project free and the client is stuck on an accepted request with no working chat.
findings.proposed_fix: In request(), handleAdminReview() and adminReview(), refuse with CLAIM_NOT_WITHDRAWABLE when the request status is in REQUEST_SETTLED_STATUSES or the slot has an ACCEPTED quote (check under the existing FOR UPDATE). In markDelivered, also require the winner slot to be OFFER_SENT. In the frontend, hide the withdraw form when ctx.quote?.status === 'ACCEPTED'. Exits after acceptance should go through a dedicated cancellation flow (see the ACCEPTED dead-end finding).

findings.title: Any firm member, including EMPLOYEE_MANAGED, can withdraw the firm's claims (money plus penalty) and mark delivery
findings.description: POST /claims/:id/withdraw and POST /company/requests/:id/deliver check only company membership (Roles COMPANY_USER + CompanyApprovedGuard + companyId match) and never memberRole. Any member of the firm, including EMPLOYEE_MANAGED, can therefore withdraw any of the firm's claims, and a late VOLUNTARY_NO_REASON withdrawal consumes the credits and adds 2 company penalty points; the same member can also start the 14-day auto-complete clock. findings.title: Production email still goes to the Mailpit sink, so new users cannot verify their accounts
findings.description: Every in-tree doc up to 2026-09-17 shows production SMTP pointing at a Mailpit sink (old public `mailpit`, planned EU `green-mail`). The config.schema production guard matches only the exact hosts mailpit/localhost/127.0.0.1/::1, so the FQDNs mailpit.railway.internal and green-mail.railway.internal boot without error, and MailService never checks the transport at boot. Login rejects unverified emails and there is no admin way to verify an account manually, so real users cannot finish registration or reset a password, and firms get no email notifications. Verification and reset links pile up in the Mailpit inbox, which only the holder of the basic-auth credential can read.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) PO: choose an EU SMTP provider (Brevo, Postmark EU or SES eu-central-1) and add SPF, DKIM and DMARC for the MAIL_FROM domain. (2) Set SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS and SMTP_SECURE=true on BOTH app-blue and app-green. (3) Harden config.schema superRefine for NODE_ENV=production: reject any host whose first label is 'mailpit' or whose port is 1025, and require SMTP_USER+SMTP_PASS. (4) Call transporter.verify() at boot, log-only with safeErrorSummary. (5) Add an admin 'send test email' action. (6) After cutover, delete the public Mailpit service and its domain, since its mailbox holds live reset links.

findings.title: Blocked-account email says 'reply to this email', but it comes from a no-reply address with no Reply-To

findings.title: Terms acceptance is stored only as a timestamp with no version, and legacy or pre-final-text accounts are never asked to re-accept
findings.description: Registration stores only users.terms_accepted_at (a timestamp) and does not record which Terms or Privacy version was accepted. Accounts created before L0-A have NULL, and neither login nor /auth/me checks the field. Every current user accepted texts that still contain [DENUMIRE LEGALĂ FIRMĂ]/[CUI]/[ADRESĂ] placeholders, so when the real texts ship the platform has no record of who accepted what and no way to require re-acceptance: it relies only on the "continued use means acceptance" clause, which is weak for material changes such as the credit and refund rules.
findings.proposed_fix: Add users.terms_version (and privacy_version) plus a LEGAL_VERSION constant in shared. Return needsTermsAcceptance from /auth/me when the stored version is below the current one (or NULL), and show a blocking re-accept modal that calls POST /auth/accept-terms (audited). Bump the version when the placeholders are replaced.

sprint_name: Sprint 3 - Legal invoicing and firm terms (P0 + bundled P1)
title: Make invoicing legally compliant and safe to launch
headline: Make invoices legal before taking real payments
goal: Report paid invoices through RO e-Factura, and block invoices or bank-transfer instructions while seller data is still a placeholder or Stripe is in test mode.
value: Firms get valid invoices reported to ANAF, never with fake seller data or from test payments.
do_first: Ask the accountant which e-Factura route to use: SmartBill/Oblio/FGO API, direct ANAF upload, or monthly export.
steps: Seed seller fields empty and add a billing-ready check: non-seed values, valid CUI checksum, valid IBAN.
Make purchases and admin confirm return 503 until billing is ready, and show a red admin banner.
Add an audited 'Date fiscale' admin form with CUI/IBAN validation, and a 'TEST MODE' banner in the wallet.
Require live Stripe keys in production unless STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_MODE, reject mismatched webhook livemode, skip invoice numbers for test orders.
Integrate the chosen e-Factura route and show each order's e-Factura status in /admin/payments.
done_when: With placeholder seller data, a purchase attempt is refused and admin shows a red banner.
Each paid order in admin payments shows its e-Factura status.
A Stripe test card cannot buy credits on production.
decision_needed: Which e-Factura route do we use: invoicing provider API (SmartBill/Oblio/FGO), direct ANAF upload, or monthly accountant export?
risks: The e-Factura route (invoicing provider API, direct SPV upload, or an accountant export) is DECIZIE NECESARA with the accountant. Invoice numbers already issued with placeholder data may need a storno outside the app.
acceptance: Purchases and admin confirm return 503 while seller_* are empty or equal the seed values, the CUI fails its checksum, or the IBAN fails mod-97, and /admin shows a red 'Date de facturare incomplete' banner
Each confirmed order shows an e-Factura status in /admin/payments, or the accountant can export the month's invoices in the agreed format
Production refuses sk_test_ keys unless STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_MODE is set, and webhook events whose livemode does not match the key mode are rejected
Test-mode orders never consume a fiscal invoice number

findings.title: Invoices are never transmitted to RO e-Factura (ANAF SPV)
findings.description: Since D-L0-1 the platform takes real Stripe payments and issues B2B invoices with a fiscal series and number to Romanian firms. The invoice exists only as a PDF re-rendered on each download: buyer data is read live, and there is no UBL CIUS-RO output, no SPV upload and no e-invoice status column. RO e-Factura reporting is therefore missing for every paid order. DECIZIE NECESARA on the fix: integrate an invoicing provider or build UBL generation plus an ANAF upload worker; a documented manual upload process by the accountant is the minimum step before launch.
findings.proposed_fix: DECIZIE NECESARA on the approach. Option 1: integrate an invoicing provider API (SmartBill/Oblio/FGO) that issues the invoice and uploads it to SPV, then store its number and PDF. Option 2: build UBL CIUS-RO generation plus an ANAF OAuth upload worker, with outbox retry and columns e_invoice_status / anaf_upload_id / anaf_download_id on the order, and show the status in /admin/payments.

findings.title: Invoices and the bank-transfer panel can go out with seed placeholder seller data; confirm() has no guard
findings.description: system_settings.seller_* is seeded with fictitious fiscal data (RO12345678, 'Str. Exemplu nr. 1', example IBAN) that the seed never overwrites, and neither PaymentsService.confirm() nor admin updateSetting validates it. The first confirmation therefore snapshots the placeholders onto a numbered invoice that the platform cannot cancel, and whose PDF presents itself as a legally valid electronic invoice. With Stripe off, the wallet also shows the fake IBAN as the transfer destination. The only protection is a manual pre-launch step in docs/08, so a billing-readiness guard (reject empty or seed values, invalid CUI checksum or IBAN mod-97) plus an admin banner is warranted.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a billing-readiness check. confirm() and both purchase endpoints refuse (503 PAYMENT_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE) when seller_* are empty, equal the seed values, the CUI fails its checksum, or the IBAN fails mod-97. Show a red 'Date de facturare incomplete' banner in /admin/settings and /admin/payments.

findings.title: Stripe test keys are accepted in production, so test-card payments would grant real credits and subscriptions
findings.description: With NODE_ENV=production, the config schema accepts sk_test_ Stripe keys: it only checks that STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are set together. The webhook handler and confirm path never check event or session livemode. So while test keys are live on the production deployment (the planned test window in rollout step 4, or a key left in by mistake), any manager of an approved firm can pay with Stripe's public test card and get real credits or subscription days, plus a real invoice number from the fiscal series. Fix: in production, require a live key unless an explicit override flag is set; reject webhook events whose livemode does not match the key mode; do not allocate fiscal invoice numbers to test-mode orders; show a test-mode banner in the wallet and admin UI.
findings.proposed_fix: In superRefine, when NODE_ENV=production require STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to start with 'sk_live_' (or rk_live_), unless an explicit STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_MODE=true is set, and set that flag only on isolated staging. In the webhook handler, reject events whose `livemode` does not match the key mode. Expose `stripeMode` in /billing/payment-instructions and show a 'TEST MODE' banner in the wallet UI when it is not live.

sprint_name: Sprint 4 - Production safety net
title: Protect production code, database and files with automated backups
headline: Back up code, database and files every day
goal: Push all production code to GitHub with CI, and back up the database and uploaded files automatically every day to a separate EU location.

findings.title: No automated backups: the only production DB dump is a manual file from 2026-09-16 on the PO's PC
findings.description: Neither production Postgres nor the MinIO uploads volume has an automated or off-site backup that the repo can show. The only copy is a manual pg_dump (cozy-preproduction-20260916.dump, 221,699 bytes) in F:\Cozy Fable\test-results\production-promotion-20260916 on the PO's PC, and future backups are planned the same manual way. There is no pg_dump or cron service, no mc mirror or versioning for the MinIO volume, no documented RPO/RTO and no recurring restore test, so every write since 2026-09-16 (requests, claims, wallets and credits, invoices, chat) exists only on the live Railway volumes.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `backup` cron service on Railway, or enable Railway scheduled Postgres backups. Daily: pg_dump -Fc, encrypt with age or gpg, upload to an off-site EU bucket (R2/B2). Retention: 30 daily + 12 monthly. Nightly: `mc mirror` the uploads bucket to the same off-site provider with versioning on. Monthly: an automated restore into a scratch DB that checks `_prisma_migrations` count and row counts, with the result emailed to the admin. Document the RPO (24h) and RTO in docs/08. Escrow the encryption key needed to read chat from a restored DB (see the slot-parity finding).

findings.title: Production file storage runs on an unmaintained bitnamilegacy/minio image with root credentials and no versioning
findings.description: Production storage runs on bitnamilegacy/minio, a frozen image that gets no security patches, as root on a single Railway volume. Its S3/admin port is reachable on a public domain. The planned EU target (green-storage) reuses the same image, and the migration plan copies the existing settings unchanged. The backend uses one S3 key pair with no bucket-scoped policy: compose maps it to MINIO_ROOT_USER, and no runbook creates a service account. There is also no versioning, lifecycle rule or volume backup, so a leaked key or a bad delete can expose or wipe every client sketch and attachment. Use the EU move to switch to a managed S3 store (R2, B2 or Railway buckets), since the community minio/minio images are no longer a maintained option either. Give it a credential limited to Put/Get/Head/Copy/DeleteObject and HeadBucket on the uploads bucket, turn on versioning with a noncurrent-version expiry rule, and set explicit CORS rules for browser PUT/GET. The app code only needs new S3_* env values.
findings.proposed_fix: As part of the EU migration, target a maintained store: official minio/minio pinned by digest, or a managed S3 such as R2, B2 or Railway buckets. Create a service account whose policy is limited to s3:GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject/HeadObject/CopyObject on the uploads bucket. Enable versioning plus a 30-day noncurrent-version lifecycle, and remove the root key from the app env. The code only changes S3_* env values.

sprint_name: Sprint 4 - Production safety net
title: Add error tracking, a split health check and safe logging
headline: See crashes and outages before users report them
goal: Let the team see real crashes, slow queries and outages as they happen, without writing customers' personal data into logs.
value: The team gets alerted on crashes and outages, and one slow service no longer takes the site down.
do_first: Add a process-only live health route and point Caddy at it instead of the deep check.
steps: 1. Make the ready health route time out each check at 1.5 seconds and return 503 only when the database is down.
2. Replace personal-data log lines with safe summaries, skip health-probe logs, and document a 7-day log retention.
3. Log the route pattern and top stack frame for every 500, and warn on queries slower than 300 ms.
4. Connect backend and frontend error boundaries to the chosen EU tracker, tagged with traceId, route and release.
5. Add cookieless analytics for wizard start and request published, name it on the Privacy page, and set uptime alerts.
done_when: A test crash on the site appears in the error tracker within a minute.
Restarting file storage no longer shows a 503 on landing or login.
Server logs contain no client addresses or emails after a failed address lookup.
decision_needed: Which error tracker and analytics do we use: Sentry EU (needs a DPA) or self-hosted GlitchTip, and Umami or Plausible?
risks: Sentry (or GlitchTip) and cookieless analytics need a DPA decision from the PO and a Privacy update. Scrubbing must reuse the existing allowlists so no request bodies or cookies leak.
acceptance: Backend and frontend errors reach an EU-hosted tracker tagged with traceId, route pattern and release SHA
Caddy routes on a process-only /health/live, and /health/ready wraps each dependency in a 1.5 s timeout and returns 503 only when the DB is down
Geo, admin-block, calendar and crypto logs no longer contain addresses, emails or raw error messages, and health probes are not access-logged
An external uptime alert watches /health/ready, and cookieless analytics record wizard_start and request_published events

findings.title: No error tracking, metrics or alerting: unknown 500s are logged as `kind=TypeError` with no stack, route or context, and outbox/queue backlog is invisible
findings.description: Neither app has error tracking, metrics or alerting. Unknown 500s are logged only as `kind=X [code] [status]` with traceId and method, and the route field resolves to 'unmatched' because pino-http binds req before routing. The frontend error boundaries only console.error or stay silent. Queue waiting/delayed depth, the domain_event_outbox backlog and the last reconciliation run are not surfaced anywhere, and no external uptime or backlog alert exists, only Railway's deploy-time healthcheck. Sentry is waiting on the PO's DPA decision, but an uptime check on /api/v1/health, the route and top stack frame (file:line) in the filter, Prisma slow-query warnings and an admin ops panel can ship without it.
findings.proposed_fix:
Add Sentry, EU data region, for Next and Nest:
- beforeSend scrubbing that reuses the safe-http/safe-error allowlists; no request bodies or cookies
- tag events with traceId, route pattern and release sha from health.release

In the filter, log the route pattern and the top stack frame (file:line only, no message). Add `prisma.$on('query')` warnings for queries over 300 ms, with model/action only. Add a lightweight /admin/ops panel showing:
- per-queue waiting/delayed/failed counts
- outbox incomplete, dead and oldest-age
- last reconciliation run

Finally, set external uptime alerts on /health/ready and an alert when outbox age exceeds 2 min.

findings.title: Health endpoint is the gateway's only routing signal, has no timeouts, and shares the app's Prisma pool, so partial degradation becomes a full-site 503
findings.description: The Caddy gateway proxies to a single upstream and routes on the deep /api/v1/health check every 10 s with a 5 s timeout. That check requires DB, Redis and MinIO to be up, with no per-dependency timeout. So one failed probe caused by a Redis or MinIO restart, a slow HeadBucket or a queued Prisma query makes Caddy return 503 for the entire site, including SSR pages and login that need neither Redis nor MinIO, until a later probe passes. Give Caddy a process-only liveness route (or drop active checks for the single upstream), and keep the deep check, with Promise.race timeouts, for Railway deploy gating and verify-slot.
findings.proposed_fix:
Split the endpoint in two:
- `GET /health/live`: process-only, returns 200 immediately. Caddy uses it for routing.
- `GET /health/ready`: deep check, each dependency wrapped in `Promise.race` with a 1.5 s timeout. It returns 'degraded' (200) when only storage or Redis is down and 503 only when the DB is unreachable. Railway deploy checks and verify-slot use it.

Run the DB probe through a dedicated tiny client or `$queryRaw` with statement_timeout so it does not queue behind user traffic. Add a synthetic uptime alert on /health/ready (see the observability finding).

findings.title: Personal data is still written to logs (addresses, emails, raw SMTP errors) with no retention policy
findings.description: The 2026-09-15 safeErrorSummary logging boundary is bypassed in four places. GeoService logs every failed Nominatim attempt with the client's street, number, city and county plus the raw error; admin block emails log the recipient address plus the raw SMTP message, which can repeat the address; and business-calendar and message-crypto log raw error text. In addition, pino autoLogging records every Caddy health probe (every 10s, about 8,640 lines a day), there is no LOG_LEVEL setting, and log retention and access remain an explicitly open operational decision while older logs may still hold signed links.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the three log lines with safeErrorSummary(e) plus non-identifying context (for example a county-level query or a hash). Add an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule banning `${e}` and `.message` in logger calls under src/. Add `autoLogging: { ignore: (req) => req.url?.startsWith('/api/v1/health') }` and a LOG_LEVEL env. Document the Railway log retention (for example 7 days) and restrict project membership.

title: Keep requests open until three firms have claimed them
headline: Keep cereri open until three firms have claimed them
goal: Let clients actually receive up to three competing offers, instead of the first offer closing the request to every other firm.
value: Clients receive up to three competing oferte instead of the first oferta closing the cerere.
do_first: Decide whether a cerere stays claimable after its first oferta while firm slots remain free.
steps: 1. Record the PO decision in the decisions log and amend invariant 3.1 on claimable statuses.
2. If slots decide, derive claimability from occupied slots below the maximum in the marketplace query and claim transaction.
3. Read the max-claims-per-request setting in the marketplace DTO and every status recompute, with a unit test.
4. If the first oferta closes claims instead, change public copy and plan-gating messages to say so.

findings.title: The first offer sent closes the request to the remaining firms (OFFERS_RECEIVED is not claimable), so clients rarely get 'up to 3 offers'
findings.description: The first offer moves the request to OFFERS_RECEIVED (quotes.service.ts:181), and neither the marketplace listing nor the claim transaction treats that status as claimable (CLAIMABLE_STATUSES = IN_MARKETPLACE/CLAIMED_PARTIAL, per invariant 3.1). Any open slots (fewer than 3 occupied) are then closed to every firm that has not claimed yet, until every sent offer is withdrawn. In a marketplace with few firms this caps the client at roughly one offer, against the public promise of up to 3 comparable offers. The code follows invariant 3.1 literally, so changing it needs a PO decision (DECIZIE NECESARA) and an invariant/decisions-log update first.
findings.proposed_fix: Needs a PO decision, then an invariant/decision-log entry. Option A: a request stays claimable while occupying slots < max and the request is not ACCEPTED or later, i.e. add OFFERS_RECEIVED/NEGOTIATION to the claimable set in 3.1, CLAIMABLE_STATUSES, the marketplace SQL, and recomputeRequestStatusAfterClaimChange. Option B: keep the status machine but decouple 'open slots' from status (e.g. a slots_open flag or a separate claimability predicate). Also decide whether a late claimant gets a fair SLA window compared with offers already sent.

findings.title: The first offer closes the remaining claim slots, so the '3 comparable offers' promise and plan gating are undermined
findings.description: Claimability depends only on request status (IN_MARKETPLACE/CLAIMED_PARTIAL, invariant 3.1). The first createQuote moves the request forward to OFFERS_RECEIVED, and it stays there while any live quote exists. So from the first offer on, the request drops out of the marketplace listing and every new claim gets CLAIM_NOT_ALLOWED, even with 1-2 of the 3 slots free and before the Gold (+30 min) and Silver (+60 min) gating windows open. This defeats the "3 comparable offers / firms compete for you" promise and the value of lower tiers. DECIZIE NECESARA: either derive claimability from occupied slots < max across the open statuses (amending invariant 3.1), or state openly that the first offer closes claims and change the copy.
findings.proposed_fix: DECIZIE NECESARA (invariant 3.1 plus business). Option A: derive claimability from the occupied slot count (< max) rather than from the request status, keeping OFFERS_RECEIVED/NEGOTIATION as client-facing progress, and update invariant 3.1 accordingly. Option B: keep the current rule but state it ('prima ofertă închide preluările') and fix the marketing copy and gating messaging.

sprint_name: Sprint 5 - Offer concurrency and three competing offers
title: Make sending and changing offers safe under concurrency and slow database
headline: Make sending offers safe when things happen at once
goal: Sending, revising, extending or withdrawing an offer can never bring back a cancelled claim, settle credits twice, or fail with a generic error because the database is slow.
value: Firms send and change oferte without random errors, double charges or double refunds of credite.
do_first: Raise the offer send and change transaction timeout to 20 seconds in the Prisma client settings.
steps: Give quote and billing write transactions longer timeouts; map slow-database and duplicate errors to retryable 503 or 409.
Route every quote action through one locked helper that re-checks status; unassign busy assignees on offer withdrawal.
Cut offer transactions to about 10 queries by building the receipt and event data from memory.
Raise serialization retries to 3-4 with jitter and wrap withdrawals and SLA/assign workers in them.
Split the quotes spec by transition; cover negotiation limits, currency conversion and races on a slow real database.
done_when: Test report shows the offer race tests passing on a real database.
'Trimite oferta' on production no longer shows 'A apărut o eroare' when the database is slow.
Withdrawing an oferta while the assignee is busy shows a clear message.
risks: Touches the core quote transactions, so a regression would block all offers; it needs integration tests against a real database before a blue/green switch.
acceptance: Racing createQuote against SLA breach, 1h auto-cancel and accept in an integration test never leaves a refunded or consumed slot as OFFER_SENT
Every quote mutation checks its allowed status inside a locked transaction and uses a conditional update; extraVersion on a WITHDRAWN or ACCEPTED quote returns 409
Quote write transactions run in at most about 10 round trips with explicit timeout options, and P2028/P2024/P2002 map to a retryable 503 or a 409 instead of 500
Withdrawing an offer when the assignee already holds another unoffered claim returns a clear 409 or unassigns the slot, never a 500

findings.title: Sending an offer can bring back a claim that was just cancelled, refunded or SLA-expired, so credits are settled twice
findings.description: createQuote checks that the slot is ACTIVE and the request is open outside its transaction. It then runs a READ COMMITTED transaction with no requests FOR UPDATE lock and moves the slot to OFFER_SENT with an unconditional claimSlot.update({ where: { id } }). So an accept, 1h auto-cancel or SLA breach that commits inside the ~1-2 s window is silently overwritten: the already refunded or consumed slot comes back as OFFER_SENT with a SENT quote, and bumpRequestStatus can move a republished request back to OFFERS_RECEIVED. A later withdrawal refund, loser CONSUME at accept or winner CONSUME at completion then settles the same reservation a second time, either minting credits or stealing another claim's reservation, or tripping CHECK reserved>=0 so accept on that request fails with a 500.
findings.proposed_fix: In createQuote, start the transaction by locking the idempotency receipt, then `SELECT ... FROM requests WHERE id=? FOR UPDATE` (Serializable + withSerializationRetry, as for claim and accept). Re-read the slot and request inside the transaction and transition with `claimSlot.updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'ACTIVE' } })`, aborting with 409 on count 0 before inserting the quote. In acceptQuote, assert that the winning slot is OFFER_SENT under the lock. Add a partial unique index on quotes(claim_slot_id) WHERE status IN ('SENT','EXPIRED'). findings.title: Other offer actions (extra version, revise, re-offer, extend, change request, withdraw offer) check preconditions outside the transaction and write statuses unconditionally
findings.description: Quote mutations other than create/accept validate their preconditions on data read before the transaction, and mutateQuote runs READ COMMITTED with no lock on the request or quote row. extraVersion never checks the quote status and always writes status 'SENT'. That reopens a WITHDRAWN quote (after a quote withdrawal, or after the claim was withdrawn and its slot closed), and the client can see and accept it. Racing an accept, it flips ACCEPTED back to SENT, so markDelivered fails forever. The other gaps are narrower: revise/reoffer/extend can add a version to a quote accepted concurrently; withdrawQuote's recompute can overwrite a competitor's concurrent OFFERS_RECEIVED with CLAIMED_* and block acceptance; and the one-PENDING-change and 2-extension caps are checked outside the transaction on endpoints with no Idempotency-Key (extend-validity, change requests, withdraw, consultation).
findings.proposed_fix: Route every quote mutation through one helper: transaction → lock receipt → requests FOR UPDATE → re-read quote, slot and latest version → assert the allowed status set per action (extra and reoffer: SENT/EXPIRED only; revise: SENT/EXPIRED and a PENDING change) → conditional `quote.updateMany({ where: { id, status: { in: [...] } } })`. Recompute request status only under the lock. Add a partial unique index on quote_change_requests(quote_version_id) WHERE status='PENDING', and check the extension cap inside the locked transaction. Put @Idempotent({transactional:true}) plus useIdempotentApi on extend-validity, change requests, withdraw offer and consultation invites, since they are limited one-shot actions.

findings.title: Serialization failures are retried only once on claim and accept, and not at all in withdrawals and the SLA/1h workers
findings.description: Claim (claims.service.ts) and accept (quotes.service.ts) run as Serializable transactions with FOR UPDATE on requests, and withSerializationRetry allows only one retry. A third firm claiming the same request within the same transaction window (a few seconds, since every query crosses regions) can therefore hit 40001 twice and get 409 CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION even though a slot is still free. Raise the retry budget to 3-4 attempts with a small random jitter, and optionally wrap the four withdrawal transactions, which currently fall through to the filter's P2034-to-409 mapping. BullMQ workers need no change: every queue already inherits attempts:3 with exponential backoff.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise withSerializationRetry to 3-4 attempts with 20-80 ms random jitter. Wrap WithdrawalsService and the SLA/assign/auto-complete processors in it. Add attempts:3 with exponential backoff to the initial SLA and assign job options, matching what the reconciliation uses when it re-arms them.

findings.title: Send-offer and quote mutations run ~30 sequential queries inside Prisma's default 5 s interactive transaction (same class as the 2026-09-17 P2028 publish outage)
findings.description: createQuote (quotes.service.ts:149) and mutateQuote (quotes.service.ts:1177, shared by revise, extra-version, re-offer, extend, withdraw and change-request) open interactive transactions with Prisma's default 5 s timeout. Because of the transactional idempotency receipt, each one runs emitQuote, participantsForQuote and the full getQuoteDto inside the transaction, about 28-30 sequential round trips at roughly 150 ms each against cross-region prod Postgres. That is the same P2028 failure class as the 2026-09-17 publish incident, which failed at 24 queries. P2028 is not mapped in AllExceptionsFilter, so "Trimite oferta" returns a generic 500 and rolls back. Fix: apply REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS-style options to quote and billing write transactions, map P2028/P2024 to a retryable 503, and move the receipt DTO and emit context out of the query-heavy path.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Give every write tx in quotes and billing explicit options, like REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS. (2) Build the idempotent receipt DTO from data already in memory, or persist a checkpoint and render the DTO after commit, instead of calling getQuoteDto (~11 RT) inside the tx. (3) Have emitQuote take requestId, companyId, title and clientUserId from the caller instead of re-querying; resolve participants with one join query. (4) In the claim tx, fold count, exclusion, own-claim and coverage into one SQL statement run with the FOR UPDATE, and read only the status column in recompute. (5) Map P2028/P2024 to a retryable 503 with a proper code. Target: at most 10 round trips per money transaction, logged in the integration spec as was done for publish.

findings.title: Withdrawing an offer fails with a 500 when the assignee already holds another active claim without an offer
findings.description: withdrawQuote moves the claim slot from OFFER_SENT back to ACTIVE with quoteId null. If the assignee has already taken another claim that has no offer yet (allowed, because assertAssignmentRules only counts unoffered ACTIVE slots), this breaks the partial unique index claim_slots_one_active_unoffered_per_assignee (P2002). The global filter does not map P2002, so the withdrawal rolls back as a 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, and the offer card's withdraw button has no onError, so the firm sees nothing while the 1-working-day withdrawal window keeps running.
findings.proposed_fix: In the withdrawQuote transaction, check whether the assignee is busy and either unassign the slot (assignedToUserId null plus a fresh assign deadline) or return 409 ASSIGNED_USER_HAS_ACTIVE_CLAIM with guidance. Also map P2002 to 409 in the global filter.

findings.title: Offer send/revise/extend/withdraw transactions still use Prisma's default 5 s timeout, which is the same P2028 risk that broke publish
findings.description:
createQuote (quotes.service.ts:149) and mutateQuote (:1177) open interactive transactions with Prisma's default 5 s timeout, because PrismaService sets no transactionOptions. On the create, revise, extra and reoffer routes marked @Idempotent({transactional:true}), the transaction also runs:
- emitQuote, about 7 queries
- a full getQuoteDto for the idempotency receipt: 8-9 QUOTE_INCLUDE relation queries plus one attachment query per version, plus an uncached settings read

That adds up to about 27-30 sequential round-trips at about 150 ms each, which is above the 24 queries that already caused P2028 on publish in prod on 2026-09-17. P2028 is not mapped in AllExceptionsFilter, which handles only P2034, so the firm gets a 500, the offer rolls back, and retries fail the same way. The mutateQuote paths without an in-tx receipt (extend, withdraw, change requests, consultations) run about 10-12 queries and are at lower risk.

Fix:
1. Pass REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS, or a shared QUOTE_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS, to both transactions, or set it globally in the PrismaClient constructor.

findings.title: Accepting an offer is not tied to the version the client saw, so a revision sent seconds earlier is accepted at the new price
findings.description: POST /client/quotes/:id/accept carries no version reference, and acceptQuote checks only the status and the latest version's validity under the lock. Meanwhile a firm can add a new version to a SENT quote at any time (reofferModify allows SENT without a client request, and so do reviseQuote and extraVersion). The client's confirm dialog shows a cached price (staleTime 30 s, no refetch on focus, no refetch after a socket reconnect, realtime delivered via the 15 s outbox sweep). So the client can irreversibly accept, and settle every other firm's credits, on a version they never saw, and no accepted_version_id is recorded.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `quoteVersionId` (the version shown in the dialog) to the accept body; it then becomes part of the idempotency hash. Under the request FOR UPDATE, compare it with the latest version and return 409 QUOTE_VERSION_CHANGED with the fresh DTO when they differ. Add quotes.accepted_version_id (migration) and use it for the post-accept summary and the PDF. In the frontend, refetch the quote when the confirm dialog opens, pass current.id, and map the new code to a message such as "Firma a trimis o versiune nouă — verifică și confirmă din nou".

findings.title: Withdrawing a claim takes one click, defaults to 'Retragere voluntară' and never states the credit or penalty cost
findings.description: The firm's 'Retrage preluarea' panel preselects VOLUNTARY_NO_REASON and withdraws on a single click, with no confirmation and no text about consequences. After the 30-minute grace, this permanently consumes the reserved claim credits and adds 2 penalty points toward the 12-point, 6-month suspension. Show the admin note on decided withdrawals and allow cancelling a pending one.

findings.title: The firm's irreversible offer and claim actions have no confirmation, show no errors, and appear when the backend will reject them; withdrawing an offer after the SLA deadline triggers an instant penalty
findings.description: In offer-card.tsx, CompanyActions never shows errors from its reject, extend, withdraw, end-negotiation or invite mutations, and there is no global onError for mutations. 'Retrage oferta' stays visible after the 1-working-day window closes and 'Prelungește' stays visible after the 2 extensions are used, so both fail with a silent 409 even though the translated messages already exist in ro.json. The penalizing or irreversible actions have no confirmation or consequence text: claim withdrawal after the 30-min grace (credits consumed plus 2 points), end negotiation (chat becomes read-only for both sides), and withdrawing an offer after the original SLA deadline+12h, which re-arms the breach job with delay 0 and costs the credits plus 3 points.
findings.proposed_fix: Expose withdrawWindowEndsAt and extensionsLeft on QuoteDto and gate the buttons on them. Add confirm dialogs that state the consequences (grace/refund vs consume + 2 points; chat closes for both sides). Render mapped ApiError messages, or add a global mutation error toast. In withdrawQuote, if the SLA deadline has passed, warn explicitly or grant a short fresh SLA (DECIZIE NECESARA).

findings.title: Withdrawing an offer re-arms the original SLA deadline and can cause an immediate SLA breach (credits + 3 points)
findings.description: When a firm withdraws an offer, the slot goes back to ACTIVE and the SLA breach job is re-queued at the original sla_deadline_at with a delay clamped to 0. The code does this on purpose (L0-B, per 4.11), but it means an offer sent late and withdrawn after deadline + 12h grace (still inside the 1-working-day withdraw window) is immediately marked SLA_EXPIRED: the claim credits are consumed and 3 SLA_MISS points are applied. The 'Retrage oferta' button calls the API directly, with no confirmation and no warning about the SLA, and a firm cannot self-revise a SENT offer, so a firm that withdraws to fix a mistake can lose the claim without knowing. The minimum fix is a confirm dialog showing the remaining SLA time (or blocking the withdrawal when deadline + grace has passed); giving the firm a fresh re-quote window after a withdrawal needs a PO decision.
findings.proposed_fix: When an offer is withdrawn, give the slot a fresh re-quote window, e.g. sla_deadline_at = max(current, now + 1 working day). This needs a one-line PO confirmation. At a minimum: block the withdrawal, or show a confirmation dialog, when deadline+grace has already passed ('după retragere ai X ore să retrimiți oferta, altfel pierzi creditele + 3 puncte').

title: Fix the wrong budget label and stop hidden problems from blocking publish
headline: Fix budget label and show what blocks publishing
goal: Published requests show the right budget, and a client who cannot publish is shown exactly which room and step to fix.
value: Firms see the real budget, and clients see which room and step to fix before publishing.

findings.title: Budget bucket stays 'Sub 5.000 RON' when the client does not touch the estimate slider
findings.description: The estimate effect in details-step.tsx sets only budgetEstimateRon. budgetRange keeps its default UNDER_5K unless the client drags the slider, because budgetRangeFromRon is called only in BudgetSlider.setRon. The backend stores that bucket and scores it verbatim, so most published requests show "Sub 5.000 RON" to firms and on the client's own page while the RON estimate is far higher, and size is misclassified in a narrow score band (for example base 25-28 becomes MEDIUM instead of LARGE). Fix: derive the bucket in the effect and on the server whenever budgetEstimateRon is present (publish and edit), then backfill existing rows and recompute their size.
findings.proposed_fix: In the estimate effect, also call setValue('budgetRange', budgetRangeFromRon(ron)). On the server, when budgetEstimateRon is present, derive budgetRange = budgetRangeFromRon(budgetEstimateRon) and ignore the client bucket, in both publish and edit. Backfill published requests where the bucket differs from the derived one, and recompute size. For flows without an estimate (DESIGN_HELP), default to UNDISCLOSED or require an explicit choice.

findings.title: Deleting a room sketch on the 'Fișiere' step leaves a dangling id that blocks publishing with no way to fix it
findings.description: On the Fișiere step (uploads-step.tsx:53-57), the client can remove any attachment, including sketches that a room's upload step still references. The server hard-deletes the file, but its id stays in that room's answers. RoomSketchUpload hides ids it cannot find and adds new uploads to the old list (room-sketch-upload.tsx:43, 63-68), so the client cannot see or clear the stale id. Publishing, or saving an edit to a published request, then fails in assertRoomAttachments with a generic 'Verifică câmpurile formularului.' error, and the only escape is deleting the whole room.
findings.proposed_fix: On the Fișiere step, show only unreferenced (project) files, reusing the review's projectFiles logic, and show room sketches read-only grouped by room. Add a store action that removes an attachment id from every room answer whenever a file is deleted. On draft load, prune upload answers against the current attachment list. On the server, return details {roomIndex, stepId} so the UI can point to the room.

findings.title: Publish validation errors are not mapped to rooms/steps, and 'completed' is never invalidated when answers change
findings.description: On publish failure the server returns CONFIGURATOR_ANSWERS_INVALID with details [{roomIndex, stepId, messageKey}] (and FLOW_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED with details {roomIndex}). The review step reads only the error code and shows copy that tells the user to check marked steps or rooms, but nothing on the review is ever marked. Review completeness relies on room.completed, which is set only by pressing Next on a room's last screen and is never reset by setAnswer. A room edited through the room chips can therefore stay marked complete after a change reveals new required steps, and the user then gets a publish error they cannot locate.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute completeness on the review with the shared validateRoomAnswers(partial:false, ownProject) per room instead of the flag. Mark invalid rooms with a 'Completează' button that jumps to the first invalid step. On a server error, use details.roomIndex/stepId to do the same.

findings.title: A nightstand placed in the Studio blocks publishing if the client picks "Pereche (2)" in the form

On the backend, return a specific error code (e.g. STUDIO_PLACEMENT_MISMATCH) with the room index, so the review step can point to the right room. Add a regression test for a Studio nightstand with count=TWO.

findings.title: Unpublishing or deleting a gallery photo leaves a hidden selection that blocks the client's publish and edit, and firms lose the reference
findings.description: If a gallery photo linked to a request or draft is unpublished or soft-deleted, the wizard still sends its id on publish or edit. assertSelectable (requests.service.ts:243,318) then rejects the whole payload with 400 NOT_FOUND, and the client sees only the generic error. The picker cannot show or remove the hidden id because it renders only what the public ?ids= query returns, so the client cannot publish that draft or edit that request, and firms silently lose that photo from the brief strip.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) In the wizard, drop ids that the ids query did not return and tell the client ('1 inspirație nu mai este disponibilă și a fost scoasă'). Alternatively, make assertSelectable on edit accept ids already linked to the request, validating only new ones. (2) Add Configurator.apiErrors.INSPIRATION_UNAVAILABLE with a dedicated error code. (3) For request-linked photos, serve firms and the owner a snapshot that skips the published filter, marked 'retrasă din galerie'. (4) In the admin, show '(N cereri active, M colecții)' before unpublishing or deleting, and add a 'Șterse' filter with a restore action. (5) Show 'X salvări nu mai sunt disponibile' on boards.

findings.title: The frontend contact caps don't account for the account email the server adds, so a guest who signs up at publish can hit an unexplained error
findings.description: A guest can save up to 4 contacts (at most 2 emails) in the details step. The rule that puts the account email in row 0 only runs inside the details step, and after login at /login?redirect=/requests/new the persisted phase sends the user straight back to review. On publish, the backend prepends the account email. If the guest entered two emails and neither matches the account email, that makes 3 EMAIL entries (or 5 contacts in total), and contactPreferencesSchema returns VALIDATION_ERROR. The review page then shows only the generic 'Verifică câmpurile formularului.' and does not point to the contacts.
findings.proposed_fix: Put a pure helper in shared, withAccountContact(contacts, email), that dedupes, prepends and trims to the caps (dropping the last extra email). Call it on the backend and in the review step before publishing, then validate with contactPreferencesSchema on the client and send the user back to the details step with the contacts highlighted when it fails.

sprint_name: Sprint 7 - Client publish and repost reliability
title: Let clients repost from any device and clear previous-user data on logout
headline: Let clients repost from any device; clear data on logout
goal: An expired request can be reposted from the logged-in account on any device, and nothing from the previous user is left in the browser after logout.
value: Clients repost expired cereri from any device; the next browser user sees none of their data.
do_first: Add a logged-in client route to repost an owned expired request, reusing the existing repost checks.
steps: Point the repost button to the new owner route and explain instead of showing it once repost is used.
Clear the draft token on publish, backfill non-draft requests, and stop storing request tokens in the browser.
Clear cached data, configurator and Studio drafts and stored tokens on logout, and disconnect realtime.
Tag saved drafts with their owner and reject publishing a draft that belongs to another user.
done_when: Expired cerere shows a working repost button on a different phone after login.
After logout and login as another user, no previous requests, address or drafts appear.
An old draft link for a published cerere shows 'not found'.
risks: Nulling draftTokenHash on published requests breaks any flow that still depends on the token route. Clearing local storage on logout discards unsaved anonymous work, so it needs clear wording.
acceptance: An authenticated POST /requests/:id/repost works from a fresh browser, and the button is hidden or explained once repostUsed is true.
After publish, GET /requests/drafts/:token returns 404 for that token, and no mm_req_token_* key is written.
After logout, the query cache is empty and mm_configurator_v1, mm_draft_token and the studio accountDraft are cleared.
Publishing a draft whose clientUserId belongs to another user is rejected.

findings.title: Reposting an EXPIRED request only works in the browser that created the draft (localStorage token)
findings.description: Repost of an EXPIRED request (business rule 4.4, one manual repost) can only be reached from the browser that published it: the button requires localStorage `mm_req_token_{id}`, and the only backend route is the public POST /requests/drafts/:token/repost. The server keeps only a hash of the token, so on another device, in incognito or after storage is cleared, the page shows no button and no explanation, even though the request.expired email sends the client there to repost. Fix: add an authenticated @Roles(CLIENT) POST /requests/:id/repost using findOwnedRequest plus the existing repost logic, point useRepostRequest at it, and hide or explain the button when RequestDto.repostUsed is true.
findings.proposed_fix: Add @Roles(CLIENT) POST /requests/:id/repost using findOwnedRequest plus the existing repost logic, and switch the FE to it. Hide or disable the button with an explanation when repostUsed. Offer 'Modifică și republică' by allowing one edit in EXPIRED as part of repost, and a 'Duplică cererea' action that clones rooms into a new draft once repost is used.

findings.title: An expired request can only be reposted from the device that created it, although the expiry e-mail says 'O poți republica din pagina cererii'
findings.description: A client can repost an expired request only from the browser that published it. The only repost route is `POST /requests/drafts/:token/repost`, the token exists only in that browser's localStorage (the backend keeps just its hash), and the detail page hides RepostButton without it. So a client who opens the 'Cererea ta a expirat' email, which promises a repost from the request page, on another device or after clearing storage has no repost option, and where the button does show it also appears after repostUsed=true. Add an authenticated owner route `POST /requests/:id/repost` that reuses the same checks and expiry scheduling (like the existing `:id/edit`), call it from the detail page, and hide the button when repostUsed is true.

Call it from the detail page regardless of the token, and hide the button when repostUsed is true, showing 'Poți crea o cerere nouă pornind de la aceasta' instead.

findings.title: Draft token is a permanent, unauthenticated bearer credential for a published request, and it stays in localStorage forever
findings.description: Publishing never clears `draftTokenHash`, and `findByToken` checks only `deletedAt`. The anonymous draft token therefore stays a permanent unauthenticated bearer credential for the published request: `@Public()` GET `drafts/:token` returns the owner DTO with address and contact values, and `edit`, `repost` and the attachment presign/confirm/remove routes keep working. None of these routes checks the owner's session, `blockedAt` or session revocation. The wizard also stores the token as `mm_req_token_<id>` in localStorage and never removes it, not even on logout, only so that `RepostButton` can call the token-based repost route, because there is no authenticated `POST /requests/:id/repost`.
findings.proposed_fix: On publish, set draftTokenHash=null in the same transaction, or have findByToken reject any status other than DRAFT. Add an authenticated owner route `POST /client/requests/:id/repost` and switch RepostButton to it. Backfill by nulling the token hashes of non-DRAFT requests. On the frontend, stop writing `mm_req_token_*` and add a one-time cleanup of existing keys.

findings.title: Logout leaves the previous user's data behind: query cache, configurator PII and draft tokens in localStorage
findings.description: useLogout only removes ['auth']. Logout is a client-side router.replace('/login') on the same long-lived QueryClient, and the query keys are not scoped to a user, so the previous user's requests, chat, quotes, billing and notifications stay cached and can be shown to the next account that logs in on that tab. mm_draft_token, mm_configurator_v1 (details with addressText, county/city and contactPreferences, plus studioScenes), mm_req_token_* and mm_studio_v3.accountDraft all survive logout; the wizard reuses the old draft token and pre-fills the details form from it. Publish then re-binds clientUserId to whoever publishes, with no check against the draft's original owner, so the next user can publish the previous user's draft, address and contacts under their own account. Fix: on logout (and on a login where the user id changes), call qc.clear(), reset the configurator store and the studio accountDraft, remove the draft and request tokens, or tag the persisted blobs with an ownerUserId and discard them on a mismatch.
findings.proposed_fix: On logout: qc.clear(), then setQueryData(['auth','me'], null); reset the configurator and studio stores; remove DRAFT_TOKEN_KEY and `mm_req_token_*`; disconnect the socket singleton. Store an ownerUserId in the persisted blobs and discard them when it does not match the logged-in user.

sprint_name: Sprint 8 - Abuse and fraud hardening
title: Restore per-user rate limits and add account lockout
headline: Stop one attacker from locking everyone out of login
goal: Rate-limit people by their real IP address, and add a per-account limit on failed logins, so one attacker can neither lock everyone out nor guess one account's password from many machines.
value: Real users stop getting random login blocks, and no account can be brute-forced from many machines.
do_first: Send a spoofed X-Real-IP header to production and check logs to confirm Railway's edge overwrites it.
steps: Key the throttler on the real client IP, via a custom tracker or Caddy trusted_proxies for Railway edges.
Move throttler storage to Redis so limits hold across restarts and blue/green switches.
Add a per-email failed-login counter: 10 failures in 15 minutes trigger cooldown, same error, notification email, stricter for admins.
Limit change-password to 5 per minute per user, and add a rate-limit check to the post-deploy slot verification.
Return 200 with no user from /auth/me when no session cookies exist, so anonymous pages skip refresh.
done_when: Audit log shows different IP hashes for different visitors.
Ten wrong passwords for one email trigger a cooldown message.
Browsing public pages logged out produces no failed auth requests in logs.
risks: Trusting the wrong forwarded header would let attackers spoof their IP, so check first that Railway's edge overwrites it. Moving the throttler to Redis changes limit behaviour across blue/green slots.
acceptance: After deploy, audit_logs show many distinct ip_hash values and verify-slot fails when req.ip is a private or edge address
Throttler storage is in Redis, and 10 failed logins for one email within 15 minutes trigger a cooldown with the same error returned either way
change-password is limited to 5/min per user
An anonymous page view no longer makes failing /auth/me plus /auth/refresh calls

findings.title: Per-IP rate limiting is keyed on a Railway proxy address, not the client IP (verified live); no per-account login lockout
findings.description: Throttling keys on the Railway edge address, not the client IP. Caddy (no trusted_proxies) overwrites X-Forwarded-For with its peer's address, Next's rewrite proxy (no xfwd) passes it through unchanged, and Nest's `trust proxy 'loopback'` makes that address req.ip, which the default ThrottlerGuard tracker uses as the in-memory bucket key. As a result, the 5/min login and 100/min global limits of invariant 3.13 apply per edge node: attackers get about 5 login attempts per minute per edge node, with no per-account lockout, and legitimate users behind the same edge node share buckets and will hit spurious 429s on login, refresh and general API calls at launch traffic. Audit-log IPs are also meaningless.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the throttler on the real client IP: a custom ThrottlerGuard.getTracker that reads Railway's edge-set X-Real-IP (after confirming the edge overwrites it). Or configure Caddy `trusted_proxies` for Railway edge ranges with `client_ip_headers X-Forwarded-For` and have Nest trust exactly that chain. Add a Redis per-email failed-login counter (for example 10 failures/15 min → cooldown, uniform error). Move throttler storage to Redis so limits survive slot switches. Add a post-deploy check to verify-slot.mjs: 3 sequential calls must show a decreasing x-ratelimit-remaining.

findings.title: Login protected only by an in-memory per-IP throttle: no per-account lockout, even for admins
findings.description: Login brute-force protection is only the @nestjs/throttler per-IP limit of 5 per minute, which uses the default in-memory store and resets on every deploy or restart. There is no per-email failed-attempt counter, progressive delay or temporary lock, and 2FA is off by decision Î10. As a result, credential stuffing from rotating IPs is not capped per account, including for ADMIN accounts, which can confirm payments, grant subscriptions and block users. Fix: back the throttler with the existing Redis. Add a per-email failure counter in Redis with progressive delay or a short lock plus a notification email, give ADMIN a stricter policy, and add a dedicated throttle to change-password, which is currently covered only by the global 100/min.
findings.proposed_fix: Back the throttler with Redis storage, since Redis is already present. Add a per-email failure counter in Redis with progressive delay or a 15-minute lock after N failures, plus a notification email. Apply a stricter policy to ADMIN logins, and throttle change-password to 5/min.

findings.title: Every anonymous page view makes two failing auth calls (GET /auth/me 401, then POST /auth/refresh 401)
findings.description: Every public page mounts PublicHeader, which calls useMe (GET /auth/me). For an anonymous visitor that request returns 401, and because /auth/me is not in NO_RETRY_PATHS, api() then calls POST /auth/refresh, which also returns 401 ('Missing refresh token'). Each anonymous page load therefore sends two failing requests, and these count toward the refresh throttle of 30/min. That throttle is per req.ip, and behind the Caddy gateway and the Next rewrite this is probably a shared proxy IP, so busy anonymous traffic can make signed-in users' real refreshes return 429 and log them out. Suggested fix: the refresh cookie path /api/v1/auth covers /auth/me, so /auth/me can return 200 {user:null} when neither the access cookie nor the refresh cookie is present, and 401 only when a refresh cookie exists and a refresh could succeed.
findings.proposed_fix: The refresh cookie's path /api/v1/auth covers /auth/me, so the server can tell the two cases apart. Return 200 {user:null} from /auth/me when neither the access nor the refresh cookie is present, and 401 only when a refresh cookie exists. The frontend then refreshes only on a real expiry. Alternatively, add '/auth/me' handling with a code check (for example NO_SESSION).

sprint_name: Sprint 8 - Abuse and fraud hardening
title: Close the free-refund loopholes and limit who sees client contact data
headline: Stop firms copying client contacts and refunding their credits
goal: Firms can no longer claim a request, copy the client's contacts and get their credits back for free, and client contacts and files are shown only to the people and claims that need them.
value: Firms pay credite to get client contacts, and staff or past claimers see only what they need.
do_first: Choose when firms see client contacts: after 30 minutes, after first message, or cancel free refund.
steps: Record the PO decision in the decisions log and apply the chosen contact-reveal or grace-refund rule.
Grant CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H only when the firm's last message is 48h old and unanswered; time-limit REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM.
Show client contacts and full address to managed employees only on claims they took or were assigned.
Hide contacts on completed claims older than the warranty window from everyone except owner and manager.
Return a redacted summary for withdrawn, expired or lost claims, and only a tombstone for deleted cereri.
done_when: Decisions log shows the chosen contact and refund rule.
Employee account sees no phone or address on colleagues' claims.
Lost or withdrawn claim page shows only title, city, status and own oferte.
decision_needed: Should contacts show only after 30 minutes or the firm's first message, should revealing them cancel the free refund, or should free refunds be capped monthly?
risks: It narrows final decisions W1 and Î18 and rewrites the 4.15 refund formulas, so it needs a PO decision (DECIZIE NECESARA) before coding; stricter rules may annoy honest firms if the wording is unclear.
acceptance: PO decision recorded in docs/07 on when contacts are revealed and when grace or 48h refunds apply
CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H is granted only when the firm's last in-app message or clarification is at least 48h old and unanswered; REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM has a time window
GET /quotes/by-claim for a withdrawn, expired, lost or deleted-request slot returns only a redacted summary with no attachments, answers or scenes
An EMPLOYEE_MANAGED member who is neither claimer nor assignee does not receive client contacts or the full address

findings.title: Client contacts and full address can be harvested for free: 30-minute full-refund withdrawal and a 48h 'unresponsive' refund that never requires the firm to have reached out
findings.description: getClaimContext shows the client's name, phone/email and exact address as soon as a claim is ACTIVE, and a VOLUNTARY_NO_REASON withdrawal within 30 minutes refunds the credits in full with no penalty and no per-company counter, cap or admin visibility. An approved firm can therefore repeatedly claim, copy the contacts and withdraw, which bypasses the credit model, the platform's only revenue. CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H also falls back to slot.createdAt and never requires a firm message, so a firm that contacts the client off-platform still gets an auto-approved refund. Fixing this means narrowing the combined effect of final decisions W1 and Î18, so the PO must choose the fix.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one or more: (a) reveal phone/email/exact address only after the 30-minute grace window or after the firm's first chat message or offer; (b) make grace refunds unavailable once contacts were revealed (store contact_revealed_at on claim_slots); (c) limit grace refunds per company per 30 days. For CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, require a firm message or clarification and measure 48h from the firm's last unanswered message.

findings.title: Every member of a firm, including EMPLOYEE_MANAGED staff, can read client contacts on all of the firm's claims
findings.description: GET /quotes/by-claim/:id (getClaimContext) checks only slot.companyId === ctx.companyId before returning the client's name, every contact channel and the full address. Consider returning client contacts and the address to EMPLOYEE_MANAGED only on slots where they are claimedBy/assignedTo (this needs CurrentUser in the controller, since CompanyContext has no userId). Any retention cutoff for COMPLETED slots needs a PO decision (DECIZIE NECESARA), because W1 grants visibility to the whole firm.
findings.proposed_fix: Return client contacts and the full address to EMPLOYEE_MANAGED only when they are claimedBy or assignedTo on that slot (OWNER/MANAGER/TRUSTED keep full access). For COMPLETED slots older than the warranty window (for example 24 months), hide contacts from everyone except OWNER/MANAGER.

findings.title: After a claim closes, or after the client deletes the request, the firm keeps indefinite access to the project files and details
findings.description: GET /quotes/by-claim/:claimSlotId (QuotesService.getClaimContext) checks only that the slot belongs to the company. It checks neither request.deletedAt nor whether the slot is still occupying (ACTIVE/OFFER_SENT/COMPLETED). findings.proposed_fix: For non-occupying slots, return a redacted summary: title, city, final status and the firm's own quote history, with no presigned attachments, room answers or scenes. When request.deletedAt is set, return only a tombstone. The claims list can still show the row.

sprint_name: Sprint 19 - Fair deadlines and pre-loss warnings
title: Fix the business calendar and let admins add holidays
headline: Count all Romanian holidays in firm deadlines
goal: Count Romanian public holidays correctly in all deadlines and let admins add bridge days or adjust sizing weights without a deploy.
value: Firms are never penalised on public holidays, and admins add bridge days without a developer.
do_first: Add 6 and 7 January to the holiday list and a test for a claim on 2026-01-05.
steps: 1. Switch holiday detection to the date-holidays library for Romania, covering 6-7 January and Easter automatically.
2. Add an admin calendar page to add or remove bridge days, refreshing both live servers.
3. Move 2025-2030 movable holidays into a data migration and alert when next year has none.
4. Add table-driven calendar tests for legal holidays, winter time, time-change days and the seed horizon.
5. Add an admin sizing-weights editor with a preview of how recent requests would be classified.
done_when: A claim made on 5 January 2026 gets a deadline of 12 January.
Admin adds a bridge day and new deadlines skip it without a restart.
Admin changes sizing weights and sees a preview before saving.
risks: Changing the calendar shifts deadlines already scheduled, and both slots must refresh together.
acceptance: A claim on 2026-01-05 gets an SLA deadline that skips 6-7 January, covered by a unit test
Holidays come from date-holidays('RO') plus an admin CRUD at /admin/calendar that refreshes both slots
A test fails when no movable holidays exist for next year, and DST/EET end-of-day cases pass
Sizing weights are editable from admin with a preview

findings.title: Business calendar misses the legal holidays of 6-7 January, ignores Decision 6 (date-holidays), seeds movable holidays only up to 2028, and has no admin override
findings.description: BusinessCalendarService uses a hand-written FIXED_HOLIDAYS set that omits 6 and 7 January, both Romanian public holidays since 2024. Every working-day calculation (3/5-day SLA deadlines, 5-day request and republish expiry, the quote-withdrawal window, clarification extensions) therefore treats them as working days. For example, a claim made on Mon 2026-01-05 gets an SLA deadline of Thu 01-08 instead of Mon 01-12, which exposes firms to SLA-miss penalties. The code also departs from Decision 6 and invariant 3.3: date-holidays is not used, movable holidays are seeded only through 2028, and there is no admin endpoint to add government bridge days or force a working day, so refresh() is only ever called at boot.
findings.proposed_fix: Add 1-6 and 1-7 to the fixed holidays, or better, use date-holidays('RO'), which covers Orthodox Easter and Pentecost automatically. Keep business_calendar_holidays for bridge days only, add admin CRUD (GET/POST/DELETE /admin/calendar) that calls calendar.refresh() on both slots, and add a unit test for 2026-01-06.

findings.title: Business calendar tests are not checked against the legal holiday list and miss winter time, DST and seeded Easter dates
findings.description: BusinessCalendarService.addWorkingDays drives every SLA, expiry and withdraw-window deadline. Yet its spec has only 5 hand-picked cases, all in July or Nov-Dec 2026. None of them checks the statutory holiday list, and that gap is how 6-7 January (reported separately) went unnoticed. There is also no test for winter time (EET) or the DST switch days (2026-03-29, 2026-10-25), for the seeded movable holidays (e.g. Thu 9 Apr 2026 + 1 working day should be Tue 14 Apr), or for the seeded Easter/Whit Monday data running out after 2028. Add a table-driven spec that checks a list of statutory holidays per year kept in the repo, loads the seed's MOVABLE_HOLIDAYS through the mocked findMany, adds EET/DST end-of-day checks (e.g. 2026-01-15 ends at 21:59:59.999Z), and adds a guard test that fails when no movable holidays are seeded for next year.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a table-driven calendar spec fed by a checked-in list of the statutory holidays per year, plus DST and winter cases and a seed-horizon guard. Load the seed's MOVABLE_HOLIDAYS through the fake businessCalendarHoliday.findMany.

headline: Warn clients and firms before deadlines hit

steps: Schedule a client reminder 2 working days before expiry, sent only while the cerere is still unclaimed.
Schedule a firm warning 30 minutes after claim if no one is assigned yet.
Schedule an SLA warning 24 hours before the deadline, sent with an email template.
Give each reminder a fixed job id and reconciliation so restarts neither duplicate nor lose it.
Add a 'De făcut acum' card on both dashboards linking offers, deliveries, unassigned claims and near SLAs.
