findings.title: Documented timed nudges are not implemented: request-expiry reminder at 3 working days, assignment warning at +30 min, SLA 'expiring soon'
findings.description: Three documented timed nudges are not implemented: the client reminder for a published request with no claim at 3 working days, i.e. 2 before the 5-day expiry (docs/03 4.4); the +30 min warning to the firm before an unassigned claim is auto-cancelled at 1h (4.9, final decision D2); and the sla.expiring_soon event, which docs/02 lists as a minimum event. The event type is declared but never published, and ASSIGN_WARNING_MS was deleted as dead code. The code comment calls the warning an 'open PO decision', which contradicts D2. As a result, requests expire without prompting the client, and firms get no push notice before an SLA miss costs them the reserved credits and 3 penalty points; they only see the deadline if they open the claim page.
findings.proposed_fix: Add delayed jobs with deterministic jobIds plus reconciliation branches: request-expiry-reminder (expiresAt minus 2 working days, only while IN_MARKETPLACE), claim-assign-warning (+30 min, only while unassigned), sla-warning (sla_deadline_at minus 24h, only while ACTIVE and not paused). Each emits a targeted outbox event with an email template. Record the +30 min decision in docs/07 if the PO really reopened it.

sprint_name: Sprint 19 - Fair deadlines and pre-loss warnings
title: Warn firms before they lose a claim and show correct countdowns
headline: Warn firms before they lose a claim
goal: Firms get a reminder 30 minutes before an unassigned claim auto-cancels and before an SLA deadline, and the worksheet shows real time left instead of 'chiar acum'.
value: Firms get a reminder before a claim auto-cancels or its SLA expires, and see real time left.

steps: 1. Replace worksheet countdowns with a future-aware formatter refreshed every minute, including 'termen depășit — mai ai X h de grație'.
2. Show SLA dates in app language and Bucharest time: amber near deadline, crimson in grace, hidden after offer sent.
3. Add a +30-minute job warning OWNER/MANAGER by bell and email if the claim is still unassigned.
4. Add SLA reminders 24h before deadline and at grace start to assignee and OWNER/MANAGER; skip paused claims, re-arm via sweep.

Absolute SLA dates use next-intl with Europe/Bucharest, and a unit test covers future dates

findings.title: No warning before an SLA breach or before the 1h auto-cancel ('sla.expiring_soon' is declared but never emitted)

Write outbox events targeted to the assignee + OWNER/MANAGER with a stable eventKey; send bell + email, deep-linked to /marketplace/claims/{id}.

findings.title: Future deadlines render as 'chiar acum'/'just now': the claim auto-cancel timer and SLA countdown are wrong
findings.description: useRelativeTime only handles past times. It computes max(0, now - then), so every future timestamp becomes 0 minutes and displays as "chiar acum"/"just now". The claim workspace WorkBar uses it for the 1-hour assign deadline, so an unassigned claim shows "preluarea se anulează automat chiar acum" for the whole hour and still after it expires. It also uses it for the SLA deadline, which shows "chiar acum" under the absolute date instead of the time left, and the text never refreshes on a timer. The fix is a future-aware formatter (next-intl format.relativeTime with useNow({updateInterval})) that shows the remaining time and switches to warning/expired styling near and past the deadline.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a useTimeUntil helper built on next-intl format.relativeTime(date, { now }). It should produce 'în 42 de min' / 'in 42 min' and should tick every 30-60 s with a small interval, or use useNow({updateInterval}). Use it for assignDeadlineAt and slaDeadlineAt. Style the text amber under 15 minutes left and crimson once expired. Add a unit test for future dates.

value: Firms only get client phone or email after paying to claim, keeping the 3-firm cap meaningful.

findings.title: Pre-claim free text (title, description, room notes, item descriptions) is shown unfiltered, so contact details can leak and bypass paid claims
findings.description: Rule 4.2 limits client contact data to firms that hold an occupying claim, but the API enforces this only for the structured contactPreferences. Before claim, every firm in radius receives the "Mesaj pentru firme" description (list and detail), the free-text questionnaire answers and the item descriptions exactly as the client typed them, and nothing checks them for phone numbers, emails, URLs or WhatsApp handles. A client who writes "sunati-ma la 07xx..." gives the contact to every eligible firm for free, which bypasses paid claims and the 3-firm cap. Fix: add an unanchored detector in shared (the existing RO/INTL phone regexes are anchored with ^$, so they can't be reused as they are). Then either block with an inline hint at publish/edit, or mask matches in the marketplace DTO.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a shared detectContactInfo(text) (RO/intl phone, email, URL, 'whatsapp' keywords) and run it at publish/edit on title, description and text answers. Either block with an inline message to the client ('datele de contact se adaugă la pasul Contact și ajung doar la firmele care preiau') or mask the matches in the marketplace DTO ('[contact ascuns până la preluare]'). Log hits for admin review.

findings.title: Firms can find a client's home before claiming: 0.1 km distance plus freely editable firm locations and radius allow trilateration
findings.description: Before any claim, the marketplace list and detail return distanceKm to 0.1 km, computed from the request's exact Nominatim point (which is street or house level when resolvable) to the nearest firm location, and they filter visibility by `dist <= coverage_radius_km`. Any OWNER/MANAGER of an approved firm can add or PUT locations with arbitrary client-supplied lat/lng and a radius down to 0.1 km, with no audit, count cap, cooldown or server-side geocoding. By moving a location and re-reading the distance, or by binary-searching the visibility edge, a firm can find a client's home to roughly 100 m without claiming, even though the full address is otherwise gated to occupying claims (W1 / rule 4.2). Fix: run pre-claim geometry on a snapped point (e.g. lat/lng rounded to about 1-2 km, or the locality centroid) in both the SQL and assertCoverage, return distance in whole km or bands, set a minimum coverage radius, and add @Audit plus a cap on location create, update and delete.
findings.proposed_fix: Run all pre-claim geometry on a coarsened point: store approx_lat/approx_lng snapped to about a 2 km grid (or the locality centroid), use it in the marketplace SQL and in claims.helpers haversineKm, and keep the exact point for post-claim only. Expose distance as whole km or bands (<5, 5-15, 15-30, 30+). Enforce a minimum coverage radius (for example 5 km), cap locations per plan, audit location create/update/delete, add a cooldown on edits, and flag firms with frequent location churn in /admin.

findings.title: Client photos, sketches and PDFs reach all eligible firms before claim with EXIF GPS and original filenames intact, and the client is not warned
findings.description: Request attachments (room photos, sketches, project PDFs) go from the browser to storage unchanged. The scan only compares size and MIME type and checks the filename for "malware". Nothing re-encodes images or strips EXIF/PDF metadata, and the original filename is kept both in the DTO and in the storage key. The marketplace detail returns these files as presigned URLs, with the original filename, to every firm that can see the request before it claims it. That exposes GPS coordinates (common in photos uploaded from a desktop) and names or addresses in filenames or PDF title blocks. Neither the upload copy nor the privacy policy tells the client this; the policy says request data reaches only firms that claimed it.
findings.proposed_fix: In the scan worker, re-encode image/jpeg|png|webp with sharp (rotate() then strip metadata) into the sealed key before marking SAFE, and serve a neutral filename (for example 'bucatarie-schita-1.jpg') to firms while keeping the original only for the owner. Also downscale on the frontend before upload (createImageBitmap + canvas.toBlob) to strip EXIF early. Add a line to uploads.subtitle and the review step: 'Fișierele sunt vizibile firmelor din zonă înainte de preluare — nu include nume, adresă sau telefon în planuri.'

findings.title: Pre-claim free text lets clients' phone numbers reach every firm, bypassing the claim
findings.description: Before a claim, the marketplace list and detail send every eligible firm the request's free-text fields unfiltered: title, description (up to 5000 chars), room answers and item descriptions. Nothing detects or masks phone numbers, emails or URLs in these fields; RO_PHONE_REGEX/INTL_PHONE_REGEX in shared validate only the contactPreferences fields. A client who writes their number in the description is exposed to every firm in range, which breaks the Terms/docs/03 4.2 promise that contacts are visible only to firms with an occupying claim, and lets firms skip paying credits.
findings.proposed_fix: At publish/edit, scan description, answers and item descriptions for phone, email and URL patterns. Warn the client in the details step, and mask the matches in the marketplace DTO (e.g. '[contact ascuns până la preluare]') while keeping the originals for occupying firms. Optionally flag repeat offenders to admin.

findings.title: Privacy policy misstates actual processing: geocoding 'on our servers' actually goes to OpenStreetMap's public Nominatim, and phone and pre-claim file visibility are omitted
findings.description: The privacy policy (ro/en.json privacy.sections) says geocoding is done 'on our servers', but GeoService sends the street address, city and county to NOMINATIM_BASE_URL, which defaults to the public nominatim.openstreetmap.org (also in .env.example), a third party. Its sharing section says request data goes 'exclusively' to firms that claimed the request, yet every eligible firm in the coverage area sees the title, description, city/county, rooms, sketches/snapshots and 3D scenes before any claim (business rule 03 §4.2 limits only contact channels to firms holding the claim), and the account email is always added as a contact whatever the client chooses.

Keep this text in sync with the review-step copy.

findings.description: The only in-product note on data visibility is one sentence on the configurator review step (review.facts.contactVisibility). sprint_name: Sprint 21 - Money-path tests and transaction policy
title: Test the money path against a real database
headline: Test credit money flows against a real database
goal: Add automated tests that run claims, withdrawals, acceptances and credit settlement against a real Postgres, so money bugs are caught before release.
value: Double refunds, double charges or stuck credite get caught by automated tests before any release.
do_first: Add a guard to integration test setup that refuses any database host except localhost or the CI service.
steps: 1. Add typed test factories and standard fake timers next to the non-local database guard in integration setup.
2. Write a credit-settlement integration spec covering claim, withdraw, auto-cancel, SLA breach, accept, completion and client delete.
3. Write a concurrency spec firing parallel claims on the last slots and parallel accepts, asserting one settlement each.
4. Add characterization tests for sizing, trials, subscription guard, marketplace gating and firm approval.
5. Return base score from sizing, add table-driven claim-cost tests, enable coverage floors, and drop the unused credit_cost column.
done_when: CI report shows credit-settlement and concurrency tests passing on a real database.
Coverage report lists billing, claims and cereri above the agreed floor.
Running tests against a non-local database stops with a clear refusal.
risks: Integration tests need a guard so they can never run against a shared or production database. Parallel race tests can be flaky unless they are seeded carefully.
acceptance: credit-settlement.integration.spec covers claim, withdraw (<30 and >=30 min), auto-cancel, SLA breach, accept with losers, completion and client delete, and asserts the ledger balances per company
Parallel claims on the last slots produce exactly max slots and one settlement each, and two parallel accepts produce exactly one ACCEPTED
Integration setup refuses any TEST_DATABASE_URL host other than localhost or the CI service
Coverage is collected with a floor on billing, claims and requests, and sizing/creditCostFromBaseScore have table-driven tests

findings.title: Credit ledger is never settled end-to-end: every money test mocks the wallet, and no DB test takes a claim to a terminal state
findings.description: No test runs the credit ledger (RESERVE → REFUND/CONSUME) against real Postgres. The 7 CI integration specs never create a claim_slot or a claim-related credit_transaction. All claim, withdraw, quote, SLA and fulfillment specs mock `credits` and the tx client, and ClaimsService.create's reserve path is never executed (its spec also passes `eventBus` where the constructor expects OutboxService). Add a DB-backed credit-settlement integration spec covering claim → withdraw (<30 and ≥30 min), unassigned auto-cancel, SLA breach, accept with losers, completion and client delete. It should assert Σ RESERVE = Σ(REFUND + CONSUME) + reserved per company and exercise the partial unique indexes and the wallet CHECKs.
findings.proposed_fix: Add apps/backend/src/modules/claims/credit-settlement.integration.spec.ts, reusing the existing TEST_DATABASE_URL harness pattern (see checkout-recovery.integration.spec.ts). Construct real CreditsService, PenaltiesService, ClaimsService, WithdrawalsService, QuotesService and FulfillmentService with stub queues and outbox, and drive cases (a)-(i) above. Finish with a shared `assertLedgerBalanced(companyId)` helper that checks both wallet columns against Σ credit_transactions. Also fix the claims.service.spec constructor order so a happy-path unit test can run.

findings.title: Claim and accept races are never tested against a real database
findings.description: No test runs the credit-moving concurrency paths against real PostgreSQL. These paths are the Serializable claim with FOR UPDATE on requests, the Serializable quote accept, the withdraw/SLA/assign settlements guarded by a conditional updateMany, and the non-negative wallet CHECK constraints. They are covered only by mocked unit tests that fake P2034 or `count: 0`, while the 7 CI integration specs cover idempotency, soft-delete, storage, tokens, checkout recovery, write-rooms and uploads. Add a TEST_DATABASE_URL integration spec that runs N+k parallel claims on the last slots, two parallel accepts on one request, and double withdraw / withdraw vs accept. It should assert slot counts, a single credit settlement, wallet totals, and that the single-retry policy does not turn legitimate claims into 409 CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION.
findings.proposed_fix: Add claims.concurrency.integration.spec.ts on TEST_DATABASE_URL: seed one request with max_claims_per_request slots and N firms with wallets, fire N+3 parallel claim calls, and assert exactly max slots are CLAIMED and the sum of reserved credits equals the slots claimed × cost. Add a parallel accept of two offers on one request (exactly one ACCEPTED, losers CANCELLED_REQUEST_ACCEPTED, credits consumed once), a double withdraw, and withdraw vs accept. The existing CI integration step runs them.

findings.title: Test harness weaknesses: untyped positional mocks, almost no fake timers, no coverage measurement, no disposable-DB guard
findings.description: Backend specs build services with positional `any` mocks under a blanket eslint-disable (8 spec files), so constructor drift goes unnoticed. For example, claims.service.spec.ts passes `eventBus {publish}` as the 4th argument, where ClaimsService now expects OutboxService (`outbox.record`). Only 3 of about 89 test files use fake timers, even though claim gating, SLA, auto-complete and penalty rules all depend on time. No jest or vitest config and no CI step collects coverage, so modules with no specs at all (penalties, marketplace, companies, admin, sizing, chat service) stay invisible. The 6 TEST_DATABASE_URL integration specs create companies, users and credit packages with no local-host guard, unlike scripts/house-acceptance.cjs. CI is safe because it points them at an isolated compose Postgres, but a misconfigured local run could leave test rows in a shared or production database, including a visible 10-credit package.
findings.proposed_fix: Add typed test factories (makeClaimsService({ prisma, outbox, ... }) returning jest.Mocked<T>) and enable the no-explicit-any lint rule for specs. Standardise jest.useFakeTimers/setSystemTime for time rules. Enable `--coverage` with per-directory thresholds for modules/{claims,quotes,billing,penalties,marketplace,chat}. In a shared integration setup, refuse any TEST_DATABASE_URL whose host is not localhost/127.0.0.1/a CI service name, and wrap each spec in a dedicated schema or transaction.

sprint_name: Sprint 21 - Money-path tests and transaction policy
title: Set one transaction policy and map transient database errors
headline: Show 'server busy, retrying' instead of generic errors
goal: Give every database transaction a sensible timeout and retry, and show 'server busy, retrying' instead of a generic error when the database is briefly slow.
value: When the database is briefly slow, publish, offers and payments retry instead of failing with a generic error.
do_first: Give the payment confirmation transaction a 20-second timeout instead of the 5-second default.
steps: Add one transaction helper with read, write and critical profiles setting timeout, isolation and retry, keeping claims at 10 seconds.
Replace all direct transactions with the helper and add a lint rule banning bare transactions outside infra.
Shorten the payment lock by moving reads before it and give cancel and admin grant 20-second timeouts.
Map database timeouts and lost connections to a 503 'server busy' code with RO/EN text and warn logs.
Make idempotent form submits retry once after two seconds on 'server busy'.
done_when: A simulated slow database shows 'Serverul e ocupat, reîncercăm' instead of a generic error.
Error logs list database timeouts as warnings, separate from real bugs.
Two payments confirmed at the same time both succeed without an error.
risks: Longer timeouts hold locks longer, so the claim timeout from invariant 3.1 must stay at 10 s.
acceptance: A runTx(profile) helper sets isolation, timeout and serialization retry, and bare $transaction is banned outside infra
P2028, P2024, P1001 and P1017 map to 503 SERVICE_BUSY with Retry-After and a warn-level log
useIdempotentApi retries once on SERVICE_BUSY

findings.title: Transaction timeouts, isolation and retry policy are scattered across modules ahead of the EU migration
findings.description: About 37 of the backend's 51 prisma.$transaction calls run on Prisma's default 5 s interactive-transaction timeout, because PrismaService sets no global transactionOptions. Per-module constants cover the rest (CLAIM_TX_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s imported across modules, REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS = 20 s used only in requests), while the app-to-Postgres link is still cross-region at ~150 ms per round trip until the EU migration, which is only proposed. A P2028 timeout is not mapped by AllExceptionsFilter, so it surfaces as a generic 500, the same failure as the 2026-09-17 publish outage; also, 7 of the 10 Serializable transactions have no withSerializationRetry, so they return 409 without retrying. Fix: centralise the options in a config-driven runTx helper (or at least set PrismaClient transactionOptions and map P2028 to a retryable error), keep the 10 s claim timeout required by invariant 3.1, and apply the serialization retry to all Serializable paths.
findings.proposed_fix: Add infra/prisma/tx.ts with runTx(profile: 'read'|'write'|'critical', fn). Each profile bundles isolation, timeout/maxWait from config (env-tunable per region), a serialization retry and the idempotency lock. Replace the direct calls and ban bare $transaction with an ESLint rule outside infra.

findings.title: Transient database errors (P2028 timeouts, lost connections) reach users as generic 500 errors
findings.description: AllExceptionsFilter gives special handling only to P2034. Transient database failures (P2028 transaction timeout, P2024 pool timeout, P1017 lost connection, and P1001, which usually arrives as PrismaClientInitializationError) are logged as unexpected errors and returned as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR, so they cannot be told apart from real bugs in logs or alerts. About 30 interactive transactions still use Prisma's default 5 s timeout, so this will happen again while the app and Postgres sit in different regions. Map these codes to a 503 with a dedicated retryable error code (plus Retry-After) and log them at warn level. Optionally, let useIdempotentApi retry once, which is safe because it already reuses the same key on 5xx and every @Idempotent endpoint is transactional.
findings.proposed_fix: Map P2028, P2024, P1001 and P1017 to 503 with a new ERROR_CODES.SERVICE_BUSY (retryable: true in details), with RO/EN copy 'Serverul e ocupat, reîncercăm'. Let useIdempotentApi retry once after 2 s for that code. Log `kind=... code=...` as today.

findings.title: Payment confirmation transaction still uses Prisma's 5 s default that already broke publish on prod
findings.description: PaymentsService.confirm() opens a $transaction with no timeout/maxWait option, so it runs on Prisma's 5 s default. Inside it make about 11-15 sequential round-trips: FOR UPDATE, re-read, a pg_advisory_xact_lock on `invoice:{series}`, aggregate, updateMany, re-read, subscription findFirst+update, wallet upsert+update+ledger insert, members, outbox. At the documented ~150-200 ms/query cross-region latency that is about 2-3 s, and every confirmation queues on the same series lock. Two or three near-simultaneous confirmations, or a latency spike, can therefore push it past 5 s into P2028 (500 INTERNAL_ERROR). Fix: pass explicit options like REQUEST_WRITE_TX_OPTIONS ({ maxWait: 5_000, timeout: 20_000 }) to confirm and cancel, and move the members read before the transaction so the advisory lock is held for less time.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass explicit tx options ({ maxWait: 5_000, timeout: 20_000 }) to confirm and to adminGrant/cancel. Move the settings reads that are already outside the tx and the members lookup out of the locked section. Consider taking the invoice advisory lock as late as possible so the serialized window is short.

sprint_name: Sprint 22 - Settle-once credits and credit rules
title: Guarantee each credit reservation settles exactly once
headline: Make sure every claim's credite settle exactly once
goal: Move all credit refunds and consumptions into one service, and add a database rule plus a daily check so a claim's credits can never be settled twice or drift from the wallet.
value: Firms' paid credite can never be refunded or charged twice, and mismatches alert admins daily.
do_first: Run a read-only production query listing claim slots with more than one refund or consume entry.
steps: 1. Fix the SLA-breach job to release at most the reserved amount and still mark the slot breached.
2. Create one settlement service that alone refunds or consumes credite, and move the seven callers onto it.
3. Add a lint rule banning direct refund or consume calls, and a shared list of credit reasons.
4. Add unique indexes so each slot has one reservation and one settlement, and validate both wallet checks.
5. Add a daily reconciliation check comparing ledger totals with wallets that alerts admins on any mismatch.
done_when: Admin Jobs page shows no failing SLA-breach jobs.
The daily ledger check reports zero wallet mismatches.
Overdue claims are marked SLA breached and the firm is notified.
risks: Existing duplicate settlements on production would make the unique index migration fail, so a read-only duplicate query must run first.
acceptance: A single ClaimSettlementService.settle() is the only caller of credits.refund/consume, enforced by an ESLint rule
A partial unique index on credit_transactions(claim_slot_id) exists for RESERVE and for REFUND/CONSUME
A daily reconciliation check compares ledger sums with wallets and alerts admins on mismatch
Both wallet non-negative CHECK constraints are VALIDATED

findings.title: Credit settlement rule (each reservation settled exactly once) is enforced only by convention in 7 files
findings.description: CreditsService.refund/consume take any amount, a free-text `reason: string` and a slot id, and never check that the slot still holds a live reservation. The "settle each reservation exactly once" rule is re-implemented by hand at 10 call sites in 6 files: withdrawals' private closeSlot(), inline conditional updateMany in claim-assign/sla-breach/fulfillment/deleteForClient, and an unconditional update that is safe only under FOR UPDATE + Serializable in acceptQuote. The outbox `refunded` flag is set by hand in each path (and left out of the SLA-breach payload), and nothing at the DB level stops a second REFUND/CONSUME for the same slot. Centralise this in one settle(tx, slotId, {from, to, outcome, reason: CreditReason}) entry point that returns `refunded` for the payload, add a partial unique index on credit_transactions(claim_slot_id) WHERE type IN ('REFUND','CONSUME') as a DB backstop, and do this before the pricing round 4 adds new settlement paths.
findings.proposed_fix: Create a ClaimSettlementService (claims or billing) with a single entry point: settle(tx, slotId, { from: ClaimSlotStatus[], to, outcome: 'REFUND'|'CONSUME', reason: CreditReason }). It performs the conditional update, writes the ledger row and returns the outcome that the outbox payload uses for `refunded`. Make refund/consume private to it, and replace the reason strings with a shared CreditReason enum (which also feeds the future credit statement UI). Add an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule that bans `credits.refund|consume` outside this service. Migrate the 7 files, then build the pricing-round-4 rules on top of it.

findings.title: No database constraint or automated check that each slot is settled once and wallets match the ledger
findings.description: The database does not enforce the per-slot rule "one RESERVE, then exactly one REFUND or CONSUME", because credit_transactions has only non-unique indexes on company_id and claim_slot_id. Everything rests on the app-level settlement tickets plus the NOT VALID CHECK >= 0, and that check misses a double settlement hidden by other reservations. Nothing automatically verifies the ledger identities (per company: balance + reserved == sum(GRANT) - sum(CONSUME); no terminal slot with an unsettled RESERVE). The hourly reconciliation worker only re-arms timers, and IMPACT credite §7 leaves these as a manual check. Fix: after a read-only duplicate query on prod, add partial unique indexes on credit_transactions(claim_slot_id) for RESERVE and for REFUND/CONSUME. Then add a daily ledger-vs-wallet check to the reconciliation worker that excludes seed-demo wallets and alerts admins.
findings.proposed_fix: First run a read-only query for slots that already have more than one REFUND/CONSUME. Then add an additive migration: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON credit_transactions(claim_slot_id) WHERE type IN ('REFUND','CONSUME'), and a matching one WHERE type='RESERVE'. Add a daily check to the reconciliation worker: per company ledger sum vs wallet, and terminal slots with RESERVE but no settlement. On mismatch, raise an admin notification and a log alert. Cover it with an integration spec on real Postgres.

findings.title: Claim cost has no upper bound, is hardcoded in shared, and silently depends on sizing weights that have no admin UI
findings.description: Claim cost is creditCostFromBaseScore = max(1, ceil(baseScore*1000/1000)), with no upper bound and with CREDIT_VALUE_RON hardcoded in packages/shared rather than in system_settings. With the seeded weights, a basic L-shaped PAL kitchen scores about 19 credits and a U-shaped kitchen with an island scores about 38. Either one costs more than Silver's 15 included credits, and a multi-room request (up to 50 rooms) can cost hundreds. The base score comes from project_sizing_config, which the code comment and docs/03 4.5 describe as editable from Admin, but there is no admin endpoint or UI for it. As a result the PO cannot tune the per-credit value, add the proposed 3..25 clamp, or adjust weights without a deploy, and any direct DB weight edit silently reprices every new request.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the credit value and min/max clamp into system_settings (credit_value_ron, claim_cost_min, claim_cost_max) read by SizingService, and show the clamp in the admin creditCostNote. Add a read-only admin view of project_sizing_config first. Make it editable only with a warning that the change affects the cost of new requests.

findings.title: Invoice buyer data is read live at download time and loses the buyer's RO VAT prefix
findings.description: Only seller_snapshot is persisted at confirm(). findings.title: Invoice document gaps: UTC date, no quantity/unit price, no service period, generic filename, link breaks after token expiry
findings.description: The invoice date is formatted with toLocaleDateString('ro-RO') and no timeZone, and neither Dockerfile.app nor railway.json sets TZ. The date is therefore UTC, so payments made between 00:00 and 03:00 Bucharest time are dated the previous day, which on the 1st of a month or 1 Jan can put them in the wrong VAT period or year, against invariant 3.3. The PDF says it complies with art. 319 but has a single line with no quantity, unit or unit price excluding VAT, and subscription lines omit the plan tier and the period covered. The file is always served as 'factura.pdf', and the wallet opens it with a plain <a href> that bypasses api()'s 401-refresh, so after 15 idle minutes (access cookie maxAge = 15 min, refetchOnWindowFocus=false) the new tab shows a raw JSON 401.

Name files factura-{serie}-{numar}.pdf. Download through api() as a blob, or refresh the session before opening. Add a 'Achitată cu cardul la {paidAt}' note.

findings.title: Dashboard 'Disponibile' credits contradict the wallet, and the wallet shows the same number twice
findings.description: Reserving credits already moves them out of balance (balance -= n, reserved += n), so balance is the free amount and getWallet returns available = balance. The company dashboard stats compute available = balance - reserved, which subtracts reservations twice: a firm with 10 free and 8 reserved credits sees 2 on the dashboard, 10 on the wallet and marketplace, and the dashboard number goes negative when reserved exceeds balance. The wallet page shows 'Disponibile' (available) and 'Sold liber' (balance), which are always the same number, and it never shows the total held (balance + reserved).
findings.proposed_fix: Change companies.service.ts:192 to available: balance and add a unit test. Change the wallet metrics to Disponibile (balance), Rezervate în preluări (reserved) and Total deținut (balance + reserved), with a one-line tooltip explaining reservation.

findings.title: Wallet ignores the viewer's role and blocked states (employees, suspended, not approved)
findings.description: The wallet page ignores the member's role and the company status. Buy/activate buttons show for every member, but purchases, checkout, orders and payment-instructions are OWNER/MANAGER only (403 FORBIDDEN). findings.title: Bank-transfer path: the promised email is never sent, there is no proforma, pending orders never expire, and bank transfer cannot be chosen when Stripe is on
findings.description: In bank-transfer mode (Stripe off), when the IBAN is missing the wallet tells firms "you'll receive payment instructions by email". Nothing sends that email: payment.pending goes only to ADMIN users as an in-app notification and is not in EMAILED_EVENTS. The firm never gets a proforma to give its accountant, because an invoice exists only after CONFIRMED. Bank PENDING orders never expire (only Stripe's checkout.session.expired and a manual admin cancel close them), and the buy-credits hint claims "secure card payment (Stripe)" even when Stripe is off.
findings.proposed_fix: Email the firm's OWNER/MANAGER the transfer details plus a proforma PDF (the invoice template marked 'Factură proformă', without a fiscal number). Auto-cancel bank orders after N days, with a reminder first. Add an 'Am plătit' action with optional OP upload that pings admins. Make the hint text conditional. Optionally offer 'Plătesc prin OP' alongside Stripe.

sprint_name: Sprint 73 - Pricing data model (P3)
title: Prepare the data model for the new pricing
headline: Make pricing plans editable data, not hard-coded rules
goal: Make plans, features and claim costs configurable data with one entitlements service, so the new pricing (free tier, plan features, capped claim cost) can be built.
value: Admins can create plans, including free ones, and change claim costs without a developer sprint.
do_first: Send the final pricing in writing: free tier, plan prices, tool features, claim-cost limits.
steps: 1. Record the approved pricing in docs/07 as a new decision replacing Î7, Î8, D-v6-5 and D-L0-2.
2. Store plan tiers and plan features as data so admins can create plans, including 0-lei plans.
3. Build one entitlements service with a feature guard; use it in subscription guard, wallet, admin KPI and frontend.
4. Let firms claim without a paid subscription where the plan allows; add claim-cost limits and recurring Stripe billing.
5. Move plan types to shared, return VAT totals from backend, and add one company-role permissions table.

Admin creates a 0-lei plan and a firma on it sees correct access.
Admin changes the claim-cost limits and new cereri respect them.

risks: The PO must first record the new pricing decision in docs/07 as superseding Î7, Î8, D-v6-5 and D-L0-2 (DECIZIE NECESARA); building before that risks rework.
acceptance: The pricing decision is recorded in docs/07
EntitlementsService.forCompany() is the single source for plan tier, gating and features, used by the guard, wallet and admin KPI
Plans and features are data (admins can create plans, including 0 lei), and claim cost has a configurable clamp
Plan and package DTO types live in shared and admin endpoints are typed

findings.title: The data model cannot express the planned pricing model (free tier, tool features per plan, capped claim cost)
findings.description: Billing implements exactly the model in docs/07: three fixed plans, claims require an active subscription, and Stripe one-off payments add 30 days to the subscription. The September pricing proposals (free tier, per-plan tool entitlements, a claim-cost clamp, recurring or annual billing) are therefore not recorded as a decision, and the schema cannot express them. Plan tier is an enum, plans have no entitlement or feature columns, admins cannot create plans or set a 0-lei price, and claim cost has no upper bound. The PO must first record the new pricing decision in docs/07 as a superseding decision to Î7, Î8, D-v6-5 and D-L0-2. After that, the entitlements, guard, clamp and billing work is an XL sprint.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the pricing decision in docs/07 first (DECIZIE NECESARA). Prerequisites: a plan entitlements/features table with a server-side requireFeature() guard and FE hook; plan tier stored as data rather than an enum; claim eligibility decoupled from 'has subscription'; a configurable claim-cost clamp in settings; Stripe Billing for recurring plans.

findings.title: Pricing and entitlement logic has no single home: the planned plan change touches ~40 backend and ~28 frontend files
findings.description: Plan entitlement logic has no single owner. The same "ACTIVE && expiresAt > now" predicate is written in SubscriptionActiveGuard (which queries Prisma directly and puts gatingDelayMinutes on the request context), in SubscriptionsService (twice) and in the admin KPI. Tier literals are cast inline even though shared already exports SubscriptionPlanTier and SubscriptionPlanDto, and admin plan/package/threshold endpoints return untyped literals that the frontend mirrors with local `tier: string` interfaces. The proposed round-4 pricing (free Start tier, plan-gated Ofertare Rapida/AI reads) would have to change every one of these places, plus the company-role checks spread across a guard, services and frontend pages. So an EntitlementsService.forCompany() plus typed admin DTOs should come before that sprint. Note that the frontend's float VAT preview (with its ?? 21 fallback) matches the backend's Decimal half-up today, because prices are Int. It would only drift if the VAT rate or prices became fractional.
findings.proposed_fix: Before the pricing sprint: (1) add an EntitlementsService.forCompany(companyId) that returns { planTier, isFree, gatingDelayMinutes, features: { quickQuote, aiReadsPerMonth } }, and use it from the guard, the wallet DTO, the admin KPI and the future PlanFeatureGuard; (2) put plan tier and plan/package DTO types in shared and type the admin endpoints; (3) have the backend return totalRon/vatRon on plan and package DTOs so the frontend stops computing VAT; (4) add a shared `can(role, action)` table for company roles and expose `permissions` on the /company/me DTO.

sprint_name: Sprint 74 - Perimeter and supply chain (P3)
title: Harden the public perimeter and software supply chain
headline: Hide internal slot addresses and patch dependencies
goal: Hide the internal slot addresses, tighten browser security rules, and keep dependencies and CI patched and scanned.
value: Attackers and search engines cannot reach old standby copies, and known-vulnerable tools leave the production image.
do_first: Make the public health endpoint return only its status, hiding the release code.
steps: Remove public slot and old gateway domains, verify releases privately, and add noindex on any non-canonical host.
Bind the backend to localhost inside the combined container through a listen-host setting.
Replace the loose CSP with per-request nonces, narrow allowed hosts, add violation reporting and COOP.
Ship only production dependencies in the image, upgrade vulnerable dev tools, and gate CI on a Trivy image scan.
Lock CI to read-only token, SHA-pinned actions, tracked Caddy image, then upgrade NestJS to 11 on standby.
done_when: Opening an old slot address in a browser no longer loads the site.
Public health page shows only a status, no release code.
CI report shows an image scan with no HIGH findings.
decision_needed: Can we remove the public Railway slot addresses and verify releases only through private networking or temporary domains?
risks: A nonce-based CSP forces dynamic rendering, and the Nest 11 upgrade can break routing, so both must be tried on the standby slot.

Nest listens on 127.0.0.1 in the combined container
CSP uses nonces with narrowed connect-src/img-src, a report endpoint and COOP

findings.title: In the combined container, NestJS listens on all interfaces, not only loopback
findings.description: In the combined Dockerfile.app container, Next proxies the API to 127.0.0.1:3001, but main.ts calls `app.listen(PORT)` with no host. Nest therefore binds to all interfaces, and any service on the Railway private network (Postgres, Redis, MinIO, Mailpit, the gateway, the other slot) can reach app-blue/app-green.railway.internal:3001 directly, skipping the Caddy gateway and the Next proxy. Auth and throttling still run inside Nest, and trust proxy 'loopback' means a direct peer cannot spoof X-Forwarded-For, so this is only hardening: add an optional LISTEN_HOST (default unset or 0.0.0.0 for dev) and set it to 127.0.0.1 in start-combined.sh, since healthchecks and all traffic already come in through Next on the public port.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an optional LISTEN_HOST to config.schema (default 0.0.0.0 for dev and compose) and set LISTEN_HOST=127.0.0.1 in Dockerfile.app/start-combined.sh; then call `app.listen(port, host)`.

findings.title: CSP allows inline scripts and any HTTPS host for connect-src and img-src, so XSS containment is nearly nil
findings.description: The production CSP in next.config.mjs allows script-src 'unsafe-inline', img-src https: and connect-src https: wss:, so it gives almost no XSS containment. An injected script could run and send localStorage data (mm_req_token_*, mm_draft_token, and the address and phone/email contacts in mm_configurator_v1) to any HTTPS host. There is no CSP violation reporting and no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, and the "Fara CSP deocamdata" comment is stale. Fix: nonce plus 'strict-dynamic' set in middleware, which forces dynamic rendering. Also narrow connect-src and img-src to self, the S3/MinIO host and the Google Maps hosts, add report-to and COOP same-origin, and update the comment.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate a per-request nonce in middleware.ts and use `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic' https://maps.googleapis.com`. Narrow connect-src and img-src to 'self', the MinIO/S3 host and maps.googleapis.com/maps.gstatic.com. Add report-to/report-uri with a small collector endpoint. Add COOP same-origin. Nonces force dynamic rendering; measure the cost on the landing page first.

findings.title: Production image ships every devDependency; pnpm audit shows 1 critical and 23 high in that toolchain, and CI never gates them
findings.description: Dockerfile.app runs a full `pnpm install` and deliberately copies the whole root node_modules store into the runtime image, only because the Prisma CLI (a devDependency) runs `migrate deploy` at boot. As a result the internet-facing container ships all dev tooling, including vitest 2.1.9, vite 5.4.21, @nestjs/cli 10, jest 29 and typescript-eslint 7. `pnpm audit` flags 1 critical, 23 high, 9 moderate and 3 low advisories in that tooling, against 1 moderate with `--prod` (@nestjs/core SSE, and no @Sse route exists). None of this code is loaded at runtime and the vitest critical needs the Vitest UI server, which this repo never runs. Still, CI gates only on `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` and never scans the image, so image scanners and compliance reviews will flag it. Fix: move `prisma` to dependencies (or use a migration image), build the runtime with `pnpm deploy --prod`/`prune --prod`, upgrade or override the dev chains, and add a Trivy/Grype scan of cozy-app:ci.
findings.proposed_fix: Move `prisma` to backend dependencies, or use a separate migration image, and build the runtime with `pnpm deploy --prod` or `pnpm prune --prod`. Upgrade vitest to ≥4.1.11 (which fixes both vitest advisories), @nestjs/cli to 11, typescript-eslint to 8 and jest to 30. Otherwise add overrides: brace-expansion ≥2.1.4/1.1.18, js-yaml ≥4.3.2/3.15.2, fast-uri ≥3.1.6, glob ≥10.5.0, picomatch ≥4.0.4, tmp ≥0.2.6. Add a Trivy (or Grype) scan of cozy-app:ci that fails on HIGH.

findings.title: CI and Dependabot hardening gaps: no token permissions block, actions pinned to mutable tags, internet-facing Caddy image not tracked
findings.description: ci.yml sets no `permissions:`, so GITHUB_TOKEN falls back to the repository default, which may be write. Its actions are pinned to mutable major tags (actions/checkout@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4), and there is no CodeQL or secret-scanning job in the repo. Dependabot's docker ecosystem only scans `/` (Dockerfile.app), so the production gateway image `caddy:2.10.2-alpine` in deploy/gateway, which proxies all public traffic behind Railway's edge, is neither digest-pinned nor tracked for updates. Fix: add `permissions: contents: read`, add a Dependabot docker entry for /deploy/gateway and pin Caddy by digest, and optionally SHA-pin third-party actions and add CodeQL.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` at the workflow level. Pin actions to full SHAs and let Dependabot bump them. Add docker entries for /deploy/gateway, /apps/backend and /apps/frontend, and pin Caddy by digest. Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection, and add CodeQL for JS/TS.

findings.title: Backend is stuck on NestJS 10; its security fixes now land only on 11.x
findings.description: The backend runs NestJS 10.4.22 for core, common, platform-express, websockets and testing, with bullmq 10.2.3 and cli 10.4.9, while @nestjs/jwt is already on 11.0.2. The one open production advisory, GHSA-36xv-jgw5-4q75 (Nest SSE field injection), is patched only in 11.1.18. It is tracked as a residual risk and is not exploitable today because the app has no SSE routes. Future Nest security fixes will likely ship only on 11.x, so each one would force an unplanned major upgrade; a planned Nest 11 / Express 5 migration, tested on the standby slot, removes that risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Plan a Nest 11 upgrade: Express 5 routing changes, @nestjs/throttler, bullmq and config compatibility, and the CLI 11 upgrade that also clears the devDependency highs. Run it on the inactive slot with the existing integration and Playwright gates.

findings.title: Direct Railway slot URLs serve a crawlable duplicate of the site (no host-based noindex)
findings.description: robots.ts (rules `allow: '/'` for every host) and the headers() function in next.config.mjs have no host condition, and neither the middleware nor the Caddy front door adds X-Robots-Tag. As a result, the public direct slot URLs (app-green-production-1223 / app-green-production-7958 .up.railway.app, which serve production data and include a standby slot on an older image that rejects writes) are fully crawlable duplicates of the site. Pages built with pageMetadata point their canonical at SITE_URL, which limits the damage, but /studio (in the sitemap), the (auth) pages and the catch-all have no canonical. Fix: add a headers() rule with `missing: [{type:'host', value:<SITE_URL host>}]` that sets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`. The slots stay reachable for the Playwright and verify-slot smoke tests, and Caddy passes the public Host header through unchanged.
findings.proposed_fix: In next.config headers(), add a rule `{ source: '/:path*', missing: [{ type: 'host', value: <SITE_URL host> }], headers: [{ key: 'X-Robots-Tag', value: 'noindex, nofollow' }] }`. Alternatively, make robots.ts return `disallow: '/'` when the request host differs from SITE_URL. Confirm with the PO that the slot URLs must stay reachable for smoke tests.

findings.title: Typography scale has drifted: 13 arbitrary font sizes, 34 ad-hoc micro-labels, inconsistent h2/h3 sizes, and mono used where the system says sans
findings.description: The frontend has no enforced type scale. Beyond .page-title/.label/.kicker it uses 13 arbitrary text-[..px] sizes (text-[11px]×53, text-[10px]×31) and 10 arbitrary tracking values. About 30 hand-written 'font-mono text-[10-11px] uppercase tracking-[..]' micro-labels duplicate .label with different sizes and colours, and h2s range from a 10px mono label to text-4xl. globals.css says labels are sans and not mono, yet Badge, table headers and Tabs are mono uppercase, and pages like the wallet have no h1 (it starts at h2 and AppShell adds none). Fix by defining a few heading and meta utility classes (or a Heading helper), moving Badge/TH/Tabs to the .label style, adding an h1 to the wallet page, and optionally linting arbitrary text-[..px] sizes.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a small type scale in globals.css/tailwind (display = .page-title; .h-section serif 22px; .h-card serif 18px; .meta 11px sans tracking .08em; .data mono 12px) and a <Heading level size> helper. Switch Badge/TH/Tabs to the .label style (keep mono for IDs and amounts only). Add an h1 to the wallet. Lint arbitrary text-[..px] with an ESLint tailwind plugin rule.

findings.title: Five hand-rolled dropdowns/popovers with no shared primitive; the account menu doesn't show who is signed in
findings.description: Five popovers each handle open state, dismissal and styling their own way: the account menu, the notification bell, the inspiration save/board picker, the board-detail move menu and the inspiration filter groups. Four use a document mousedown listener and the filter uses a fixed inset-0 backdrop button. Only the account menu and the bell close on Escape. The account menu has role="menu"/menuitem but no arrow-key navigation or focus management, and its header shows only the role label ('Firmă'/'Client'), not the user's name, email or firm, even though useMe() already returns name and email. Proposal: add Radix Popover/DropdownMenu wrappers in components/ui, migrate the five popovers to them, and show avatar, name, email and (for company users) the company name from useMyCompany in the account menu header.
findings.proposed_fix: Add @radix-ui/react-popover and @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu wrappers in components/ui with the shared panel style, and migrate the five instances. Show avatar, name, email and (for firms) the company name in the account menu header.

findings.title: Design-token hygiene: dead 'plan' alias, stale 'albastru-plan' comments, duplicate surface/card tokens, hardcoded hex values
findings.description: tailwind.config.ts defines a `plan` colour alias (same var as `walnut`) that no class uses. Its comment, plus comments in button.tsx and globals.css, still describe the brand colour as "albastru-plan" (PLANSA identity), but --walnut is brown #855232 under ATELIER. `surface` duplicates `card` (both hsl(var(--card))), and Avatar/TierBadge hardcode hex colours outside the token system (text-[#FBF6EC], tier gradients #B07F1E/#D4A547 etc.). Fix: remove the alias, correct the comments, standardise component code on one of surface/card, and move the tier/avatar colours into CSS variables.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the plan alias and fix the stale comments. Pick one of surface/card for component code. Move tier and avatar colours into CSS variables (--tier-gold-from/to, --on-walnut). Add a short docs/design-tokens.md (or a Codex note) listing the ATELIER tokens and their intended use.

sprint_name: Sprint 76 - Collections into requests (P3)
title: Let clients attach a whole collection, with notes, to a request
headline: Let clients attach whole collections with notes to a cerere
goal: Clients can add a whole collection to a request and note what they like about each photo and which room it is for.
value: Firms see which photos the client likes, why, and for which room.
do_first: Add optional note and room fields to board items and request inspiration photos in the schema.
steps: Migrate board items and request inspiration photos to hold an optional note (max 200 chars) and room link.
Add 'Adaugă toată colecția' in the configurator picker, up to the cap, carrying notes over.
Show notes and photos grouped by room to the claiming firma.
Let the gallery save button save one photo into several boards using ticks.
done_when: Picker offers 'Adaugă toată colecția' and keeps the notes.
Firm view of a cerere shows photo notes grouped by room.
One photo can be saved into two collections at once.
risks: Schema changes are needed (a note and a room link on request_inspiration_photos and board items). Share links raise privacy questions.
acceptance: The picker offers 'Adaugă toată colecția' up to the cap and carries notes over.
The firm sees notes and photos grouped by room.
The SaveButton can save a photo to several boards.

findings.title: Collections are a dead end for the request: a board cannot be attached, pins have no notes, and firms get only ≤10 bare thumbnails
findings.description: Inspiration photos reach a request only as a bare list of up to 10 IDs (request_inspiration_photos has no note or room link), and firms see only image, title and company in RequestInspirationStrip. So a client cannot say what they like about a specific photo or which room it is for, except in the request's general description. The boards tab in the configurator picker only toggles photos one by one (no "add whole board", and the board name is not carried over). The gallery SaveButton models a photo as living in one board only (move/remove), although the backend supports several boards, and boards have no read-only share link.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an optional note (≤200 chars) on board items and on request_inspiration_photos, plus an optional room link (request room id). In the picker, add 'Adaugă toată colecția' (up to the cap) that carries the notes over. Show notes and room grouping to the claiming firm. Let the SaveButton save into additional boards (a list of boards with ticks), and consider a read-only share link per board.
